related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Larger scale does not automatically improve life. Before buying, expanding, or moving, ask whether it creates real freedom or adds a longer chain of dependence and greater maintenance cost. When evaluating expansion, calculate yearly maintenance time, fixed cost, and exit difficulty, not acquisition alone; only visible long-term burden reveals whether freedom truly increases.
Retain basic life skills and nearby relationships. Preparing simple food, handling basic problems, and knowing neighbors become resilience when systems fail in ways efficiency cannot replace. Practice one basic skill and know one nearby mutual-aid contact each month; resilience comes from relationships and capacities available before crisis, not emergency searching.
Reduce meaningless comparison with distant lives and recover contact with the community at hand. Local cooperation, long friendship, and familiar places often provide satisfaction that infinite choice cannot. Replace one distant comparison with local participation through purchase, visit, or shared work; investing in reachable connection returns satisfaction from abstract options to lived community.

zh.title: 信言不美，美言不信

lineByLineTranslation: 真实可信的话不华美，华美的话不真实可信。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
真实的话不一定好听，但应该尽量清楚且少伤害。表达困难事实时，去掉夸张和羞辱，把证据、影响与需要说明白，诚实才不会成为攻击借口。困难事实要选择合适时间和私密程度，并给对方回应空间；诚实若能被接住，更可能促成改变，而不只是完成说话者的释放。
帮助别人时，判断他是否因此更有能力。代替选择、制造依赖或让对方欠人情，都可能把善意变成控制；有益的帮助最终会归还自由。每次帮助都设一个能力增长的迹象和退场节点，若对方始终无法多承担一步，就要检查援助是否正在制造新的依赖。
做决定前，用“是否有益、是否伤害”作为最后检查。收益不能只算自己得到什么，也要看代价落在谁身上；利而不害，是整部书留给行动的尺度。决策后追踪短期获益与长期外部成本，尤其听受影响最深者的反馈；利而不害必须接受结果检验，而不只相信善意。

verse: Sincere words are not fine; fine words are not sincere.
Those who are skilled (in the Tao) do not dispute (about it); the disputatious are not skilled in it.
Those who know (the Tao) are not extensively learned; the extensively learned do not know it.
The sage does not accumulate (for himself).
The more that he expends for others, the more does he possess of his own; the more that he gives to others, the more does he have himself.
With all the sharpness of the Way of Heaven, it injures not; with all the doing in the way of the sage he does not strive.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Truth may not sound pleasant, but it should remain clear and cause as little harm as possible. When stating a difficult fact, remove exaggeration and humiliation; honesty should not become permission to attack. Choose suitable timing, privacy, and room for response; honesty that can be received is more likely to create change than merely release the speaker.
When helping, ask whether the other person gains capacity. Choosing for them, extending dependence, or creating a debt can turn kindness into control; beneficial help eventually returns freedom. Give every act of help a sign of growing capacity and a withdrawal point; if the recipient never carries one step more, examine whether aid is creating dependence.
Before acting, use benefit and harm as the final check. Gain cannot count only what you receive; it must include where the cost lands. Benefiting without harm is a practical measure for the entire book. After deciding, track immediate benefit and long-term external cost, especially through those most affected; benefiting without harm must face outcome evidence, not rely on good intention.

sources.silkBTranscription: 天下□胃我大，大而不宵。夫唯不宵，故能大。若宵久矣，其細也夫！我恆有三保，市而𤥯之。一曰茲，二曰檢，三曰不敢為天下先。夫茲故能勇；檢敢能廣；不敢為天下先，故能為成器長。今舍其茲且勇；舍其檢且廣；舍其後且先；則死矣！夫茲以單則朕，以守則固。天將建之，如以茲垣之。
sources.receivedReference: 天下皆谓我道大，似不肖。夫惟大，故似不肖。若肖，久矣其细也。夫我有三宝，保而持之：一曰慈，二曰俭，三曰不敢为天下先。夫慈，故能勇。俭，故能广。不敢为天下先，故能成器长。今舍其慈，且勇。舍其俭，且广。舍其后，且先。死矣。夫慈，以战则胜，以守则固。天将救之，以慈卫之。

zh.title: 天下皆谓我大，大而不肖
reconstructedVerse: 天下〔皆〕谓我大，大而不肖。
一曰慈，二曰俭，三曰不敢为天下先。
夫慈，故能勇，俭，故能广，不敢为天下先，故能为成事长。
今舍其慈，且勇，舍其俭，且广，舍其后，且先，〔则〕必死矣。
夫慈，以战则胜，以守则固。
lineByLineTranslation: 天下人都说我的道很大，大得不像任何具体事物。
正因为不像任何具体事物，所以能够广大。
如果像某种具体事物，早就变得细小了。
我恒常有三件宝物，握持并珍惜它们。
第一叫慈爱，第二叫节俭，第三叫不敢走在天下人之前。
因为慈爱，所以能够勇敢；因为节俭，所以能够宽广；不敢走在天下人之前，所以能够成为事业的领袖。
如今舍弃慈爱却求勇敢，舍弃节俭却求宽广，舍弃居后却争先，那就一定会走向死亡。
慈爱用于作战便能胜利，用于防守便能稳固。
上天要成全一个人，就像用慈爱筑墙保护他。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
作决定前，先问能否减少伤害、减少浪费、减少抢先。慈悲让你看见影响，节俭让资源可持续，不争第一让别人也有生长空间。在方案评审中设置一栏，分别记录对最弱者、资源消耗和他人成长空间的影响，三宝才能进入决定，而不是停留在赞美。
节俭不是一味压缩生活，而是不把有限资源耗在虚荣和重复上。把钱、时间和注意力留给长期价值，个人与组织都会更有韧性。节俭后的资源要明确流向什么长期价值，否则节省容易只变成更高利润或更大扩张，没有形成真正韧性。
不敢为天下先，不等于永远退缩。必要时仍要承担，只是不把领先当作身份；先看共同需要，再决定自己站在哪个位置，以及何时应该让出位置。领先时设一个交棒条件，必要承担完成后主动让出舞台；能进也能退，才不会被“第一”的身份绑架。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 67
en.title: Compassion, Frugality, And Not Being First
verse: All the world says that, while my Tao is great, it yet appears to be inferior (to other systems of teaching).
Now it is just its greatness that makes it seem to be inferior.
If it were like any other (system), for long would its smallness have been known!
But I have three precious things which I prize and hold fast.
The first is gentleness; the second is economy; and the third is shrinking from taking precedence of others.
With that gentleness I can be bold; with that economy I can be liberal; shrinking from taking precedence of others, I can become a vessel of the highest honour.
Now-a-days they give up gentleness and are all for being bold; economy, and are all for being liberal; the hindmost place, and seek only to be foremost;--(of all which the end is) death.
Gentleness is sure to be victorious even in battle, and firmly to maintain its ground.
Heaven will save its possessor, by his (very) gentleness protecting him.

explanation.body: Beginning from “天下皆谓我大，大而不肖,” this chapter explores compassion, frugality, and not being first. It does not demand a rigid answer; it asks how conditions, opposites, limits, and timing change what wise action looks like.

explanation.title: Chapter theme
explanation.body: Compassion keeps power from requiring harm, frugality keeps resources from being consumed by craving, and not rushing to be first frees action from vanity. Together they form a bounded, durable courage.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Before deciding, ask whether harm, waste, and the need to be first can be reduced. Compassion sees impact, frugality preserves resources, and not rushing ahead leaves room for others to grow. In option review, record effects on the most vulnerable, resource consumption, and others' room to grow; the three treasures then enter decisions rather than remain admired ideas.
Frugality does not mean making life uniformly smaller. It refuses to spend limited resources on vanity and repetition; preserving money, time, and attention for lasting value builds resilience. Name the long-term value that saved resources will support; otherwise frugality may become only higher profit or larger expansion without creating genuine resilience.
Not daring to be first does not mean permanent retreat. Carry responsibility when necessary without making leadership an identity; begin with the common need, then choose the position you should occupy. Set a handoff condition when taking the lead and yield the stage after necessary responsibility is complete; entering and leaving freely prevents first place from becoming identity.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
冲突中先把目标从“赢过对方”改为“解决问题”。一旦只想获胜，事实就会被挑选、关系会被牺牲；共同面对问题，才可能保留合作。冲突开始前共同写下要解决的问题和不能牺牲的关系，讨论偏离时就回到这两项，胜负冲动才不会偷偷替换目标。
不争不是不表达。把事实、需要和边界说清楚，但不羞辱、不抢最后一句、不强迫立即同意，能让坚定与尊重同时存在，也让对话仍有下一步。表达后给对方复述和提问的时间，不用最后一句封死讨论；边界被清楚听见且仍可回应，才有机会形成真实协议。
看到别人表现更好时，把嫉妒转成信息。问自己真正向往什么、可以学习什么，而不是贬低对方；竞争可以成为成长线索，不必变成敌意。嫉妒出现时把它改写成一个学习目标和一个自己的行动，既承认向往，也把能量从评价别人收回到建设能力。

en.title: The Virtue Of Non-Contention
verse: He who in (Tao's) wars has skill Assumes no martial port; He who fights with most good will To rage makes no resort.
He who vanquishes yet still Keeps from his foes apart; He whose hests men most fulfil Yet humbly plies his art.
Thus we say, 'He ne'er contends, And therein is his might.'
Thus we say, 'Men's wills he bends, That they with him unite.'
Thus we say, 'Like Heaven's his ends, No sage of old more bright.'

explanation.body: The most skillful victory need not turn another person into a loser. Less provocation, steadier emotion, and better use of everyone's capacity can end conflict instead of merely changing the winner.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
In conflict, change the goal from defeating the other person to solving the problem. Once victory becomes primary, facts are selected and relationship is sacrificed; facing the problem together preserves cooperation. At the start of conflict, write the problem to solve and the relationship that must not be sacrificed; return to both whenever the urge to win quietly replaces purpose.
Non-contention does not mean silence. State facts, needs, and boundaries without humiliation, demanding the last word, or forcing immediate agreement; firmness and respect can remain together. After speaking, give the other person time to restate and question rather than closing with the last word; a heard boundary that can still receive response may become agreement.
When someone performs better, use envy as information. Ask what you genuinely long for and can learn instead of diminishing them; comparison can become a clue for growth rather than hostility. Translate jealousy into one learning goal and one personal action; desire is acknowledged while energy returns from judging another person to building your own capacity.

所以两军实力相当时，心怀悲悯的一方会取胜。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
进入冲突前，先记得受伤不是抽象代价。每个决定都会落在具体身体、家庭和未来关系上；保留悲悯，能防止立场让人对伤害麻木。决策文件中加入受影响者的具体生活后果，不只写抽象风险；名字、时间和恢复成本被看见，立场就较难掩盖伤害。
真正强大的人敢于承认悲伤和损失。团队或家庭经历事件后，不急着要求振作；允许哀悼，才有机会诚实整理发生了什么，并真正开始恢复。恢复期要允许生产力下降，并给哀悼明确空间；要求立刻正常，常会把未处理的损失推入身体和未来关系。
当双方都想赢时，更能看见代价的一方往往更接近成熟。愿意停止升级、保护无辜、留下和解路径，不是软弱，而是拒绝让冲突继续吞噬。停止升级时同时提出保护措施和后续谈判时间，克制不是放弃问题，而是把它从互相毁伤带回可解决范围。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 69
en.title: The Grieving Side Prevails
verse: A master of the art of war has said, 'I do not dare to be the host (to commence the war); I prefer to be the guest (to act on the defensive).
I do not dare to advance an inch; I prefer to retire a foot.'

This is called marshalling the ranks where there are no ranks; baring the arms (to fight) where there are no arms to bare; grasping the weapon where there is no weapon to grasp; advancing against the enemy where there is no enemy.
There is no calamity greater than lightly engaging in war.
To do that is near losing (the gentleness) which is so precious.
Thus it is that when opposing weapons are (actually) crossed, he who deplores (the situation) conquers.

explanation.title: Chapter theme
explanation.body: Grief in conflict is not weakness; it keeps struggle from becoming spectacle. Trustworthy strength sees the cost, restrains attack, and preserves a path back to ordinary life for both sides.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Before entering conflict, remember that harm is not an abstract cost. Every decision lands on specific bodies, families, and future relationships; compassion prevents a position from making us numb. Include concrete life consequences for affected people in decision records, not abstract risk alone; names, time, and recovery cost make harm harder for position to conceal.
Real strength can acknowledge grief and loss. After an event affects a team or family, do not demand an immediate recovery; space for mourning allows an honest account of what occurred. Allow productivity to fall during recovery and give grief explicit space; demands for immediate normality often move unprocessed loss into bodies and future relationships.
When both sides want victory, the side that can still see the cost may be closer to maturity. Stopping escalation, protecting the uninvolved, and leaving a path to reconciliation are forms of strength. When stopping escalation, also propose protection and a time for later negotiation; restraint does not abandon the problem but returns it from mutual damage to a solvable range.

zh.title: 吾言甚易知也，甚易行也
reconstructedVerse: 吾言〔甚〕易知也，〔甚〕易行也。
而人莫之能知也，〔而〕莫之能行也。
夫唯无知也，是以不我知。
lineByLineTranslation: 我的话很容易理解，也很容易实行。
可是人们没有谁能理解，也没有谁能实行。
言论有根源，行事有主宰。
正因为人们不知道这个根源，所以不了解我。
了解我的人很少，这正是我的可贵。
因此圣人外穿粗布衣，怀中却藏着美玉。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
不要因为外表普通就低估价值。一个安静的人、一项基础工作、一种不善宣传的能力，可能正是团队长期可靠的核心；判断要看作用，不只看包装。评价贡献时先问若这项基础工作停止会发生什么，依赖程度会显出被包装遮住的价值，也能纠正只奖励高曝光的偏差。
自己有能力时，也不必急着展示全部。先让事实和作品成熟，再选择合适时机表达；内在有分量的人，不需要每次都靠外界确认。为表达能力设一个真实需要，而不是每次有能力就展示；选择时机能保护注意力，也让出现的声音更值得被听见。
保持朴素，同时不要把才能藏成自我否定。怀玉不是拒绝贡献，而是不让贡献被虚荣支配；该承担时清楚站出来，完成后仍能回到平常。承担之后接受正常的感谢和回报，再回到日常；既不贪恋舞台也不拒绝价值，才能让才能持续服务而不扭曲。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 70
en.title: Coarse Clothes, Jade Within
verse: My words are very easy to know, and very easy to practise; but there is no one in the world who is able to know and able to practise them.
There is an originating and all-comprehending (principle) in my words, and an authoritative law for the things (which I enforce).
It is because they do not know these, that men do not know me.
They who know me are few, and I am on that account (the more) to be prized.
It is thus that the sage wears (a poor garb of) hair cloth, while he carries his (signet of) jade in his bosom.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not underestimate value because its appearance is ordinary. A quiet person, foundational task, or poorly advertised skill may be the core of long reliability; judge by function rather than packaging. Ask what would happen if a basic contribution stopped; the degree of dependence reveals value hidden by packaging and corrects reward systems built only around visibility.
When you have ability, there is no need to display all of it immediately. Let facts and work mature, then speak at the useful time; inner substance does not require constant external confirmation. Require a real need before displaying capacity rather than showing everything available; choosing the moment protects attention and gives the eventual voice more weight.
Remain plain without hiding talent as self-denial. Holding jade within does not refuse contribution; it keeps contribution from being ruled by vanity. Step forward when needed and return to ordinary life afterward. After carrying responsibility, receive ordinary gratitude and compensation, then return to daily life; neither clinging to visibility nor rejecting value lets talent continue serving without distortion.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
不确定时，直接说“我还不知道”。假装确定会让错误决定更难修正；承认知识边界，反而能邀请证据、专家和不同经验进入。在会议和报告中明确标注事实、推断与未知，三者不混在一句话里，后续证据出现时团队便能准确更新，而非整套结论崩塌。
知道得越多，越要看见未知仍有多大。专业判断中保留假设、条件和置信度，可以防止一句结论被误用成不容讨论的真理，也保护后来修正。专业结论要附适用条件、资料范围和最可能的误差来源，读者知道边界，知识才不会因被过度使用反而制造危险。
面对别人的问题，不必立刻给答案来证明有用。先澄清问题、说明自己知道与不知道的部分，再共同寻找；诚实的未知比漂亮的误导更可靠。没有答案时可以先提供寻找路径、可靠来源和下一次回看时间；承认未知仍能承担过程，不必用猜测填补有用感。

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
When uncertain, say directly, “I do not know yet.” Pretended certainty makes a wrong decision harder to repair; acknowledging the boundary of knowledge invites evidence, expertise, and other experience. Mark facts, inferences, and unknowns separately in meetings and reports; when new evidence appears, the team can update precisely rather than watching an entire conclusion collapse.
The more you know, the more visible the remaining unknown should become. Stating assumptions, conditions, and confidence keeps professional judgment from being misused as unquestionable truth. Attach conditions, evidence range, and likely error sources to professional judgment; knowledge becomes safer when readers understand where it stops being reliable.
You do not need an instant answer to prove usefulness. Clarify the question, state what you know and do not know, and search together; honest uncertainty is more reliable than an impressive misdirection. Without an answer, offer a search path, credible source, and next review time; responsibility for the process can remain without filling usefulness with a guess.

related.body:
了解自己，也要善待自己。看见局限后，不用羞辱和比较逼迫改变；尊重身体节奏、给错误修复空间，成长才不会建立在自我厌恶上。发现局限后把批评改写成下一步可练习的能力，羞辱只说明“你不好”，而具体练习才告诉生命可以怎样继续。
自爱需要边界。拒绝长期消耗、离开反复伤害、为休息保留时间，不是自私，而是承认生命值得被保护，也值得在清醒中继续成长。边界要提前表达并配合一致行动，不等耗尽后突然爆发；及时保护自己，也减少关系因长期隐忍承受更大破坏。

Let them not thoughtlessly indulge themselves in their ordinary life; let them not act as if weary of what that life depends on.

And thus he puts the latter alternative away and makes choice of the former.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Know yourself and treat yourself with care. After seeing a limitation, do not use shame and comparison to force change; respect bodily timing and leave room to repair mistakes so growth is not built on self-hatred. After seeing a limitation, rewrite criticism as a capacity that can be practiced next; shame says only that you are bad, while specific practice shows how life can continue.
Self-care requires boundaries. Refusing chronic depletion, leaving repeated harm, and protecting time for rest are not selfish; they recognize that life deserves protection. Express boundaries early and support them with consistent action rather than exploding after depletion; timely self-protection also prevents greater relational damage from long silence.
Do not interpret being yourself as refusing feedback. Real self-knowledge hears the impact of behavior and then chooses whether to adjust; loving yourself includes not remaining inside unconscious harm. On receiving feedback, first restate the impact the other person experienced, then choose adjustment or explanation; authenticity and responsibility together make the response genuinely self-aware.

en.title: Courage Not To Dare
verse: He whose boldness appears in his daring (to do wrong, in defiance of the laws) is put to death; he whose boldness appears in his not daring (to do so) lives on.
Of these two cases the one appears to be advantageous, and the other to be injurious.
But When Heaven's anger smites a man, Who the cause shall truly scan?
On this account the sage feels a difficulty (as to what to do in the former case).
It is the way of Heaven not to strive, and yet it skilfully overcomes; not to speak, and yet it is skilful in obtaining a reply; does not call, and yet men come to it of themselves.
Its demonstrations are quiet, and yet its plans are skilful and effective.
The meshes of the net of Heaven are large; far apart, but letting nothing escape.

explanation.title: Plain reading · Read the movement of the whole chapter
explanation.body: Beginning from “勇于敢则杀，勇于不敢则活,” this chapter explores courage not to dare. It does not demand a rigid answer; it asks how conditions, opposites, limits, and timing change what wise action looks like.

explanation.title: Chapter theme
explanation.body: Courage includes the ability not to act. With high-risk, irreversible, or harmful choices, restraint is not cowardice; it is a willingness to answer for consequences.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Courage appears not only in daring but in stopping. When information is insufficient, cost is unclear, or innocent people may be harmed, refusing impulsive action requires more stability than bravado. Before acting, test urgency through reversibility, affected people, and worst consequence; if these are unknown, reduce the scope so courage does not transfer risk to others.
Under group pressure, preserve the sentence, “I need more time to think.” Not declaring immediately or joining excitement protects judgment and gives other uncertain people room from coercion. Under group pressure, state why more time is needed and when you will answer; a bounded pause protects judgment without turning responsibility into indefinite delay.
After caution, still carry necessary action. Not daring is not avoidance of every risk; it first identifies what should not be done, then directs strength toward the responsible choice. After caution, choose one necessary and bearable action while accepting incomplete certainty; responsibility means consciously carrying remaining risk, not waiting for risk to disappear.

zh.eyebrow: 帛书乙本底本校读 · 对应今本第七十四章
zh.title: 若民恒且不畏死，奈何以杀
reconstructedVerse: 若民恒且不畏死，奈何以杀惧之也？
若民恒且畏死，而为奇者，〔吾〕得而杀之，夫孰敢矣。
若民恒且必畏死，则恒有司杀者。
夫代司杀者杀，是代大匠斲〔也〕。
夫代大匠斲〔者〕，则希不伤其手〔矣〕。
lineByLineTranslation: 如果人民恒常不怕死，怎么能用杀戮来恐吓他们？
如果人民恒常怕死，而有人作乱，我把他抓来杀掉，谁还敢作乱？
如果人民确实怕死，就恒常有专司刑杀的力量。
代替司杀者去杀，就像代替高明木匠砍削。
代替高明木匠砍削，很少有不伤到自己手的。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
不要替别人执行本应由他承担的后果。过度代办、替人解释、替人道歉，看似帮助，长期却会夺走对方学习责任的机会，也让关系越来越失衡。帮助前先问“这是谁的责任、我提供到哪里、何时交还”，三项说清，援助才不会在不知不觉中取代对方的人生功课。
拥有权力时，更要守住职责边界。不是所有错误都需要最重处罚，也不是所有问题都由你裁决；程序和角色分工能防止个人情绪变成伤害。惩处决定应记录角色权限、证据标准和申诉方式，程序把个人情绪限制在边界内，也保护正当行动的可信度。
看到不公可以介入，但先确认授权、证据和影响。越过边界去“替天行道”，容易复制自己反对的暴力；正当目的也需要正当方法。介入不公时先与受影响者确认需要，避免替别人决定何为拯救；正当方法必须让被帮助者仍拥有声音与选择。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 74
en.title: Do Not Usurp The Executioner
verse: The people do not fear death; to what purpose is it to (try to) frighten them with death?
If the people were always in awe of death, and I could always seize those who do wrong, and put them to death, who would dare to do wrong?
There is always One who presides over the infliction of death.
He who would inflict death in the room of him who so presides over it may be described as hewing wood instead of a great carpenter.
Seldom is it that he who undertakes the hewing, instead of the great carpenter, does not cut his own hands!

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not carry consequences that another person must learn to carry. Repeatedly doing, explaining, or apologizing on their behalf looks helpful but removes the opportunity to develop responsibility. Before helping, ask whose responsibility this is, where your support ends, and when it returns; clear answers prevent aid from replacing another person's necessary learning.
The more power you hold, the more carefully role boundaries must be kept. Not every error requires the strongest punishment and not every problem is yours to judge; process prevents personal emotion from becoming harm. Record role authority, evidence standards, and appeal routes for disciplinary decisions; procedure contains personal emotion and protects the credibility of legitimate action.
Intervene in injustice only after checking authority, evidence, and impact. Acting as a private executioner can reproduce the violence you oppose; a just purpose still requires a just method. Before intervening in injustice, confirm needs with affected people rather than deciding what rescue means for them; a just method preserves their voice and choice.

zh.title: 人之饥也，以其取食税之多
reconstructedVerse: 人之饥也，以其取食税之多〔也〕，是以饥。
百姓之不治也，以其上有以为也，〔是〕以不治。
民之轻死，以其求生之厚也，是以轻死。
夫唯无以生为者，是贤贵生。
lineByLineTranslation: 人民之所以饥饿，是因为统治者收取的粮税太多，所以饥饿。
百姓之所以难以治理，是因为上位者强作妄为，所以难以治理。
人民之所以轻视死亡，是因为把求生看得太厚重，所以反而轻死。
只有不刻意把生命当作私有目标的人，才真正懂得珍重生命。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
越害怕失去，越容易用控制耗损正在拥有的生命。为了健康、安全或关系不断检查和限制，可能让日常只剩防备；保护需要边界，也需要呼吸。给健康与关系的检查设合理频率，超过后若没有新事实就回到生活；控制停得下来，保护才真正服务生命而非吞噬生命。
不要把活得久、拥有多、位置高当成唯一价值。生命的质量也在真实连接、自由选择和有意义的投入里；数量不能替代活着的感受。每月回顾一项无法量化却重要的体验，例如亲密、自由或投入感，让生命价值不被数字指标逐渐挤出视野。
准备风险之后，允许自己继续生活。做必要保险、检查和计划，然后去运动、爱人、尝试；成熟不是消灭不确定，而是在不确定中保持生命力。完成准备后主动安排一件有活力的行动，把安全带回运动、连接和创造；风险管理的目的，是让生活继续展开。

en.title: Overvaluing Life Can Cheapen It
verse: The people suffer from famine because of the multitude of taxes consumed by their superiors.
It is through this that they suffer famine.
The people are difficult to govern because of the (excessive) agency of their superiors (in governing them).
It is through this that they are difficult to govern.
The people make light of dying because of the greatness of their labours in seeking for the means of living.
It is this which makes them think light of dying.
Thus it is that to leave the subject of living altogether out of view is better than to set a high value on it.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
The more we fear loss, the more control can consume the life already present. Endless checking and restriction for health, safety, or relationship can turn daily existence into defense; protection needs boundaries and breath. Set reasonable checking intervals for health and relationship, returning to life when no new fact appears; protection serves life only when control can stop.
Do not make longevity, possession, or status the only measures of life. Quality also lives in real connection, free choice, and meaningful effort; quantity cannot substitute for the experience of being alive. Review one important but unquantifiable experience each month—intimacy, freedom, or meaningful engagement—so numeric measures cannot gradually crowd life's value out of view.
After preparing for risk, allow life to continue. Arrange necessary insurance, checks, and plans, then move, love, and try; maturity does not eliminate uncertainty but preserves vitality within it. After preparation, schedule one enlivening action in movement, connection, or creation; the purpose of managing risk is to let life continue unfolding.

en.title: Softness Belongs To Life
verse: Man at his birth is supple and weak; at his death, firm and strong.
(So it is with) all things.
Trees and plants, in their early growth, are soft and brittle; at their death, dry and withered.
Thus it is that firmness and strength are the concomitants of death; softness and weakness, the concomitants of life.
Hence he who (relies on) the strength of his forces does not conquer; and a tree which is strong will fill the out-stretched arms, (and thereby invites the feller.)
Therefore the place of what is firm and strong is below, and that of what is soft and weak is above.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
A living body needs softness and room to adjust. When pain, fatigue, or emotion changes, hear the signal and alter the pace; enduring rigidly is not always strength and may reduce the ability to recover. When the body signals, lower intensity and observe recovery before total failure forces recognition; early adjustment preserves continuity at far less cost than collapse.
Views also need the capacity to bend. Revising after new evidence does not damage credibility; defending an error to preserve a consistent image makes the position increasingly lifeless. When revising a view, preserve the earlier judgment and new evidence so others can see the path of change; transparent updating builds more credibility than performed correctness.
An organization that permits only one method and voice also loses vitality. Space for experiment, dissent, and learning gives a system capacity for changes it cannot yet predict. Give experiments and dissent a safe scope, duration, and review; clear space helps people offer alternatives and converts learning into system capacity.

zh.title: 天之道，犹张弓者也
reconstructedVerse: 高者抑之，下者举之，有余者损之，不足者〔补之〕。
人之道〔则不然〕，损不足而奉有余。
孰能有余而〔有以取〕奉于天〔者〕乎？
是以圣人为而弗有，成功而弗居也。
lineByLineTranslation: 天的规律，就像拉弓。
高的压低它，低的抬高它；有余的减损它，不足的补充它。
所以天的规律，是减损有余、补充不足。
人的做法却不是这样，反而减损不足去供奉有余。
谁能把自己的有余拿出来奉献给天下？
只有有道的人吧。
所以圣人有所作为却不占有，事情成功却不居功。
他这样做，是不愿炫示自己的贤能。

en.title: Heaven'S Way Fills What Lacks
verse: May not the Way (or Tao) of Heaven be compared to the (method of) bending a bow?
The (part of the bow) which was high is brought low, and what was low is raised up.
(So Heaven) diminishes where there is superabundance, and supplements where there is deficiency.
It is the Way of Heaven to diminish superabundance, and to supplement deficiency.
It is not so with the way of man.
He takes away from those who have not enough to add to his own superabundance.
Who can take his own superabundance and therewith serve all under heaven?
Only he who is in possession of the Tao!
Therefore the (ruling) sage acts without claiming the results as his; he achieves his merit and does not rest (arrogantly) in it:--he does not wish to display his superiority.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Notice where excess and insufficiency sit before speaking of fairness. When resources always flow toward those who already hold the most, the whole loses resilience; meeting basic capacity allows everyone to participate. Before allocation, examine minimum conditions for participation and the largest unused surplus; restore access first, then discuss extra reward, so fairness increases whole capacity.
Team reward cannot see only visible outcomes. Maintenance, care, documentation, and support carry the gaps of a system; recognizing this work keeps collaboration from becoming unbalanced. Give maintenance and support their own measures and attribution in performance records; visible invisible work no longer requires exhaustion to prove its importance.
Use personal surplus to meet real lack. Handle difficult work when energy is available, build reserves when income is stronger, and reach toward others when relationship is stable; let margin flow toward the true gap. Let surplus move only when capacity truly exists and toward a named lack; giving from enough does not erase boundaries, but directs resources more accurately to need.

zh.title: 天下莫柔弱于水，而攻坚强
reconstructedVerse: 天下莫柔弱于水，〔而攻坚强者莫之能胜也〕，以其无以易之也。
柔之胜刚，弱之胜强，天下莫弗知也，而〔莫能行〕也。
故圣人之言云，曰：受邦之垢，是谓社稷之主。
受邦之不祥，是谓天下之王。
lineByLineTranslation: 天下没有比水更柔弱的，而攻击坚强之物却没有什么能胜过水，因为没有别的东西可以替代它。
柔弱胜过刚强，天下没有人不知道，却没有人能实行。
所以圣人说：能够承担国家的屈辱，才叫国家的主人。
能够承担国家的灾殃，才叫天下的君王。
正面的话听起来反像反话。

explanation.body: 水的力量来自不与坚硬比坚硬。面对难以说服的人或局面，可以持续寻找缝隙、降低对抗、改变路径；不正面碰撞，也能坚持方向。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
面对强硬局面，不必把自己变得更硬。降低对抗、改变路径、持续表达关键事实，像水寻找缝隙，能在不放弃原则的情况下保存力量。强硬回应出现前先降低音量、速度与范围，只保留必须表达的事实和边界；压力下降后，真正方向反而更容易被听见。
柔弱的作用需要时间。一次温和沟通可能看不见结果，但长期守信、稳定边界和不报复，会逐渐改变关系能够承受的范围，让防御慢慢松开。为长期温和设可观察承诺，例如不报复、按时回应和一致边界；柔弱通过重复获得力量，不靠一次沟通制造奇迹。
真正的胜利不是把对方击碎，而是让问题失去继续伤害的力量。保留转身、修复和重新合作的可能，比短暂压服更接近长久解决。解决方案要同时回答如何止损、如何修复、如何预防再发，三层都具备，胜利才不会只把问题暂时压到地下。

en.title: Water Overcomes The Hard
verse: There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it;--for there is nothing (so effectual) for which it can be changed.
Every one in the world knows that the soft overcomes the hard, and the weak the strong, but no one is able to carry it out in practice.
Therefore a sage has said, 'He who accepts his state's reproach, Is hailed therefore its altars' lord; To him who bears men's direful woes They all the name of King accord.'
Words that are strictly true seem to be paradoxical.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
A hard situation does not require making yourself harder. Lower confrontation, change the path, and continue stating essential facts; like water finding an opening, principle can remain while strength is preserved. Before answering hardness, reduce volume, speed, and scope, keeping only necessary facts and boundaries; when pressure falls, the real direction often becomes easier to hear.
Soft influence needs time. One gentle conversation may show no immediate result, but long reliability, steady boundaries, and refusal to retaliate gradually change what a relationship can hold. Give long-term gentleness observable commitments—no retaliation, timely response, and consistent boundaries; softness gains strength through repetition, not one miraculous conversation.
Real victory does not break the other person; it removes the problem's ability to continue harming. Preserving possibilities for turning, repair, and future cooperation resolves more than temporary domination. A solution should explain how harm stops, repair occurs, and recurrence is prevented; with all three, victory does not merely push the problem underground.

related.body:
有凭据、有道理，也不必把追责变成羞辱。说明事实、责任和期限，同时保留履行的路径，比反复逼迫更可能让旧账真正结束。追责开始时先确认共同认可的事实、责任范围和结束条件，程序清楚，旧账才有机会完成，而不是被反复用来控制关系。
关系里不要把每次让步都记成债。清楚重要边界，也允许善意自由发生；若所有付出都等待回报，亲近会逐渐变成结算，彼此也会失去轻松。对长期付出可直接讨论需要与边界，不靠暗中记账等待对方领悟；说得清楚，善意才不必在失望后突然翻成指控。
掌握优势时，克制追加惩罚的冲动。目标应是恢复公平和防止再犯，而不是享受对方低头；止于必要，才能避免正当追责变成报复。惩罚达到修复和预防目的后就停止，并记录为何结束；权力能自我收束，是防止正义滑向报复的重要证据。

en.title: Hold The Tally Without Demanding
verse: When a reconciliation is effected (between two parties) after a great animosity, there is sure to be a grudge remaining (in the mind of the one who was wrong).
And how can this be beneficial (to the other)?
Therefore (to guard against this), the sage keeps the left-hand portion of the record of the engagement, and does not insist on the (speedy) fulfilment of it by the other party.
(So), he who has the attributes (of the Tao) regards (only) the conditions of the engagement, while he who has not those attributes regards only the conditions favourable to himself.
In the Way of Heaven, there is no partiality of love; it is always on the side of the good man.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Having evidence and being right do not require turning accountability into humiliation. State the fact, responsibility, and deadline while preserving a path to fulfill them; this closes an obligation better than repeated pressure. At the start of accountability, agree on facts, responsibility scope, and ending conditions; clear process lets an old debt finish instead of controlling relationship forever.
In relationship, do not record every act of care as a debt. Keep important boundaries while allowing kindness to be freely given; when every contribution waits for repayment, closeness becomes an account. Discuss needs and boundaries around long-term giving directly rather than keeping a secret account for someone else to discover; clear speech keeps disappointment from becoming accusation.
When holding advantage, restrain the urge to add punishment. The purpose is restored fairness and prevention, not the pleasure of submission; stopping at what is necessary keeps accountability from becoming revenge. Stop penalty once repair and prevention are achieved and record why it ends; power able to limit itself is evidence that justice has not slipped into revenge.

zh.title: 道可道也，非恒道也
lineByLineTranslation: 可以说出的道，就不是恒常不变的道。
可以命名的名，就不是恒常不变的名。
无名，是万物开始的状态；
有名，是万物得以生长、分化的母体。
所以，恒常保持无欲，用来观察它幽微的本质；
恒常带着欲望，用来观察它显现的边界。
这两者同出一源，只是名称不同，所指相同。
幽深之中还有幽深，是通向一切微妙的门。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 1
en.title: Names Are Not The Whole
verse: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.
The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
(Conceived of as) having no name, it is the Originator of heaven and earth; (conceived of as) having a name, it is the Mother of all things.
Always without desire we must be found, If its deep mystery we would sound; But if desire always within us be, Its outer fringe is all that we shall see.
Under these two aspects, it is really the same; but as development takes place, it receives the different names.
Together we call them the Mystery.
Where the Mystery is the deepest is the gate of all that is subtle and wonderful.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not reduce a person to one name. A job title, personality label, or single mistake is only partial; in family and work, attend to present behavior so an old label does not sentence the relationship in advance. When an old impression conflicts with present facts, revise the judgment instead of forcing the person to match your memory; this keeps the relationship open to renewed understanding.
Before saying “I already understand,” give the facts more time to appear. Many misunderstandings come not from missing information but from treating a guess as a conclusion; continued observation prevents needless defense and explanation. Replace “I know” with “what I can currently observe,” separating evidence from interpretation so later facts can change the conclusion without a battle over pride.
Do not let other people's definitions become your enclosure either. You can acknowledge past choices and still respond differently today; names help communication, but they should never become the boundary of growth. When a label begins narrowing your choices, note who gave it to you and whether it still fits, then test another possibility through one small different action.

zh.title: 天下皆知美之为美，恶已
reconstructedVerse: 天下皆知美之为美，恶已。
是以圣人居无为之事，行不言之教。
万物作而弗始〔也〕，为而弗恃也，成功而弗居也。
lineByLineTranslation: 天下人都知道美之所以为美，丑也就出现了。
都知道善之所以为善，不善也就出现了。
有与无彼此生发。
难与易彼此成就。
长与短彼此显出形状。
高与下彼此充盈、映照。
音与声彼此应和。
先与后彼此跟随，这是恒常的关系。
所以圣人以无为的方式处事，以不言的方式施教。
万物兴起而不据为开端，有所作为而不依恃，事情成功也不占有功劳。
正因为不占有，成果才不会离开。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
遇到好坏、输赢、对错的争论时，先看看双方是不是在互相定义。一个方案显得快，往往因为另一个方案承担了稳定；看见代价，判断才不会只剩站队。讨论方案时把收益、代价和由谁承担分别写出来，许多看似绝对的优劣，会显出只是站位不同。
关系里的冲突常不是谁彻底错误，而是两种需要挤在同一个时刻。把立场背后的害怕、期待和边界说清楚，比急着压倒对方更可能找到完整答案。先各自复述对方真正担心什么，确认没有听错，再谈办法，能把争执从人格攻击拉回需要协调的问题。
当你只看见事情的一面，主动换到相反的位置再看一次。这样做不是取消原则，而是检查自己的结论能否容纳现实的复杂，避免用局部正确制造整体伤害。换位后仍要回到事实与底线：既看另一面，也说明哪些伤害不能接受，这样完整不等于含糊。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 2
en.title: Opposites Arise Together
verse: All in the world know the beauty of the beautiful, and in doing this they have (the idea of) what ugliness is; they all know the skill of the skilful, and in doing this they have (the idea of) what the want of skill is.

So it is that existence and non-existence give birth the one to (the idea of) the other; that difficulty and ease produce the one (the idea of) the other; that length and shortness fashion out the one the figure of the other; that (the ideas of) height and lowness arise from the contrast of the one with the other; that the musical notes and tones become harmonious through the relation of one with another; and that being before and behind give the idea of one following another.
Therefore the sage manages affairs without doing anything, and conveys his instructions without the use of speech.

All things spring up, and there is not one which declines to show itself; they grow, and there is no claim made for their ownership; they go through their processes, and there is no expectation (of a reward for the results).
The work is accomplished, and there is no resting in it (as an achievement).
The work is done, but how no one can see; 'Tis this that makes the power not cease to be.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
When people argue over good and bad, winning and losing, or right and wrong, notice how each side defines the other. A fast option may look fast because another option carries stability; seeing the hidden cost makes judgment more complete than taking sides. List each option's benefit, cost, and who must carry that cost. Many apparently absolute judgments then reveal themselves as differences in position rather than complete truth.
Conflict in a relationship is rarely proof that one person is entirely wrong. Two needs may simply be competing in the same moment; naming the fear, expectation, and boundary beneath each position creates more room than defeating the other person. Have each person restate what the other is truly afraid of before proposing solutions; accurate listening moves conflict from character attack back to needs that can be coordinated.
When only one side of a situation is visible, deliberately examine it from the opposite position. This does not abandon principle; it tests whether your conclusion can hold reality's complexity without using partial truth to create wider harm. After changing perspective, return to evidence and boundaries: understand the other side while naming harms that remain unacceptable, so complexity does not become moral vagueness.

zh.eyebrow: 帛书乙本底本校读 · 对应今本第三章
zh.title: 不上贤，使民不争
reconstructedVerse: 不贵难得之货，使民不为盗。
是以圣人之治也，虚其心，实其腹，弱其志，强其骨。
恒使民无知无欲也，使夫智不敢。
lineByLineTranslation: 不抬高所谓贤能，使人不为名位相争。
不把难得的财货看得贵重，使人不去偷盗。
不把可欲之物摆出来，使人心不被扰乱。
所以圣人的治理，是使心思虚静、腹中充实、意志不逞强、筋骨强健。
常使人少机巧、少贪欲，也使自恃聪明的人不敢妄为。
不强行作为而已，便没有什么不能治理。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
先分清“我需要”还是“我不想输给别人”。消费、升职和社交里的许多焦虑来自比较；把注意力拉回身体、时间和真实用途，欲望才不会替你做决定。把想要的东西延迟二十四小时，再问不用向任何人展示时是否仍想要，通常能分出真实需要与比较冲动。
为金钱、成绩和曝光设一条“够用线”。没有边界的追求会不断抬高门槛，让已经拥有的东西失去感受；知道何时足够，才能把精力留给真正重要的人生。“够用线”要写成可观察标准，例如金额、时间或频率；边界具体，满足才不会随着别人的成绩不断后退。
少展示一点，并不等于放弃进取。让作品、服务和长期信用自己说话，可以减少为了维持形象而产生的浪费，也让合作回到能力和价值本身。每次想证明自己时，把精力转向一个能被使用的改进，让可验证的贡献替代表演，长期更能建立可信度。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 3
en.title: Reduce Rivalry And Craving
verse: Not to value and employ men of superior ability is the way to keep the people from rivalry among themselves; not to prize articles which are difficult to procure is the way to keep them from becoming thieves; not to show them what is likely to excite their desires is the way to keep their minds from disorder.
Therefore the sage, in the exercise of his government, empties their minds, fills their bellies, weakens their wills, and strengthens their bones.
He constantly (tries to) keep them without knowledge and without desire, and where there are those who have knowledge, to keep them from presuming to act (on it).
When there is this abstinence from action, good order is universal.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
First ask whether this is a genuine need or a fear of falling behind. Much anxiety around purchases, promotion, and social visibility is comparison in disguise; return attention to the body, available time, and actual use before desire makes the decision for you. Delay the desired purchase or commitment for twenty-four hours, then ask whether you would still want it if nobody could see it; comparison and genuine need often separate here.
Set an enough-line for money, achievement, and exposure. Pursuit without a boundary keeps raising the threshold until what you already have becomes invisible; knowing what is sufficient preserves energy for the parts of life that truly matter. Make the enough-line observable through an amount, time limit, or frequency. A concrete boundary keeps sufficiency from retreating whenever someone else achieves more.
Showing less does not mean abandoning ambition. Let work, service, and long-term trust speak for themselves; this reduces the waste of maintaining an image and brings collaboration back to real capacity and value. Whenever the urge to prove yourself rises, redirect that energy into one improvement another person can actually use; verifiable contribution builds trust more durably than display.

en.title: Useful Emptiness
verse: The Tao is (like) the emptiness of a vessel; and in our employment of it we must be on our guard against all fulness.
How deep and unfathomable it is, as if it were the Honoured Ancestor of all things!
We should blunt our sharp points, and unravel the complications of things; we should attemper our brightness, and bring ourselves into agreement with the obscurity of others.
How pure and still the Tao is, as if it would ever so continue!
I do not know whose son it is.
It might appear to have been before God.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not schedule life until it has no room to breathe. Leave transition between tasks, silence inside relationships, and a night before major decisions; open space reveals fatigue and allows a wiser response to arrive. Real space must be protected on the calendar rather than expected to appear after busyness ends; reserve recovery and transition first so urgent requests cannot consume them forever.
When solving a problem, ask not only what must be added but what layer can be removed. One less approval, defensive explanation, or unused feature may serve the real need better than another pile of resources. Clarify the essential purpose before removing a layer. This prevents necessary support from being cut while ensuring that simplification genuinely serves the people using the system.
Leaving room for change is mature design. Plans, budgets, and commitments should not work only under ideal conditions; a system with margin can absorb surprise instead of transferring every shock to the people inside it. Write alternatives for delay, illness, or missing resources into the plan in advance; margin then becomes a structure that can absorb reality rather than a hopeful intention.

关心一个人，不等于替他取消事实和后果。家庭、团队和公共事务中，把同情与判断分开，才能既看见处境，也不让偏爱伤害其他人。可以同时说“我理解你为何这样做”和“这件事仍需承担后果”，两句话并存，关怀就不必以牺牲公平为代价。
当事情没有按照个人愿望发展，先别把它解释成命运针对自己。世界有自己的条件和节奏；接受这一点，能把抱怨省下来的力量用于真正可改变的部分。把不可控制、可影响、可立即行动的部分分开，只处理后两项，能让接受现实转化为有效行动而非消极认命。

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Caring for someone does not mean cancelling facts or consequences on their behalf. In family, teams, and public decisions, separating compassion from judgment lets us understand circumstances without allowing favoritism to harm others. Say both “I understand why you did this” and “the consequence still needs to be carried.” Holding these sentences together prevents compassion from purchasing fairness with someone else's loss.
When events do not follow personal wishes, resist reading them as the world targeting you. Reality has conditions and timing of its own; accepting that returns the energy of complaint to what can actually be changed. Separate what cannot be controlled from what can be influenced and what can be done now; acting on the latter two turns acceptance into effective response rather than resignation.
Fairness is not indifference; it asks whether a rule survives an exchange of roles. Before setting a boundary or distributing resources, ask whether you would still accept the arrangement from the other position. Before setting a rule, examine it from the positions of beneficiary, burden-bearer, and most vulnerable participant; role exchange exposes costs your first perspective may have ignored.

related.body:

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Protect the source that allows you to create for a long time. Sleep, solitude, bodily rhythm, and uninterrupted time may look unproductive, yet they determine whether giving remains sustainable instead of becoming proof through exhaustion. Each week identify one activity that restores energy and one that steadily drains it, then increase the first and reduce the second; this makes care for the creative source concrete.
Stable strength is rarely loud. Rather than waiting for a burst of motivation, build a small practice that can be repeated daily; continuous modest nourishment changes life more reliably than occasional intensity. Shrink a practice until it remains possible on a tired day, and track continuity rather than intensity; durable strength is formed inside repetitions too ordinary to impress anyone.
Love also needs a source within relationship. Do not confirm your worth only by being needed; a person who can restore alone and connect outward can give without controlling and leave without punishing. Before giving, ask whether you genuinely consent and have capacity, and allow the answer to be no; voluntary care carries fewer hidden invoices for repayment later.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
After accomplishing something, share credit with the people who truly carried it. Naming other contributions does not diminish you; it strengthens continued ownership and keeps the result from depending on one person's image. During review, name the specific difficulty each person solved rather than offering general thanks; precise recognition brings invisible labor into the team's shared memory.
Transfer methods, authority, and essential information. If every decision must wait for you, responsibility has become dependence; durable work can still operate clearly during your absence. Test a handoff by asking whether another person can complete the work independently once; documentation without rehearsal may still leave essential knowledge locked inside the former owner.
Not centering yourself does not require exhausting yourself. Long service needs boundaries and restoration; help that is not traded for approval is less likely to harden into resentment or hidden control. Before helping, state the time, scope, and ending conditions. This protects capacity and lets the recipient understand how temporary support will gradually return responsibility.

zh.title: 上善如水

水善于利益万物，并且保持安静。
它停留在众人厌恶的低处，
所以接近于道。
居处以合宜之地为善，内心以深静为善，
给予以顺应天时为善，言语以真实可信为善，
治理以安定有序为善，做事以发挥所长为善，
行动以切合时机为善。
正因为不争，所以没有过失和怨尤。

en.title: The Goodness Of Water
verse: The highest excellence is like (that of) water.
The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things, and in its occupying, without striving (to the contrary), the low place which all men dislike.
Hence (its way) is near to (that of) the Tao.

The excellence of a residence is in (the suitability of) the place; that of the mind is in abysmal stillness; that of associations is in their being with the virtuous; that of government is in its securing good order; that of (the conduct of) affairs is in its ability; and that of (the initiation of) any movement is in its timeliness.
And when (one with the highest excellence) does not wrangle (about his low position), no one finds fault with him.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Learn to take the lower place when it is useful. Listening first, gathering facts, and understanding another person's difficulty do not reduce dignity; like water moving low, the one who can receive often sees the whole more clearly. Ask three questions you genuinely want answered before presenting your solution; this turns taking the lower place into operational listening rather than a performance of politeness.
When resistance appears, do not answer immediately with greater force. en.title: Step Back When Complete
verse: It is better to leave a vessel unfilled, than to attempt to carry it when it is full.
If you keep feeling a point that has been sharpened, the point cannot long preserve its sharpness.
When gold and jade fill the hall, their possessor cannot keep them safe.
When wealth and honours lead to arrogancy, this brings its evil on itself.
When the work is done, and one's name is becoming distinguished, to withdraw into obscurity is the way of Heaven.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
When a result already serves its purpose, pause before adding more. Extra features, promises, or polish can turn an achievement into burden; knowing when it is enough is part of protecting its value. Define a clear completion standard, then change only what materially affects use; without a stopping condition, improvement easily shifts from serving value to soothing anxiety.
After completion, deliberately make room for others. Transfer visibility, decision-making, and opportunities to grow; this tests whether the result can stand alone and prevents past success from becoming your enclosure. Making room must include real authority and resources, not verbal encouragement alone; successors need permission to decide and make recoverable mistakes before growth space is genuine.
Complete the ending before leaving: explain the current state, preserve the method, and disclose the risks without making everyone permanently dependent on you. A good exit enables continuation rather than simply disappearing. A complete ending also names the new owner, review date, and escalation path, turning “it can continue” from a hopeful sentence into an accountable arrangement.

en.title: Holding To One And Mysterious Virtue
verse: When the intelligent and animal souls are held together in one embrace, they can be kept from separating.
When one gives undivided attention to the (vital) breath, and brings it to the utmost degree of pliancy, he can become as a (tender) babe.
When he has cleansed away the most mysterious sights (of his imagination), he can become without a flaw.
In loving the people and ruling the state, cannot he proceed without any (purpose of) action?
In the opening and shutting of his gates of heaven, cannot he do so as a female bird?
While his intelligence reaches in every direction, cannot he (appear to) be without knowledge?

(The Tao) produces (all things) and nourishes them; it produces them and does not claim them as its own; it does all, and yet does not boast of it; it presides over all, and yet does not control them.
This is what is called 'The mysterious Quality' (of the Tao).

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Before an important commitment, notice whether body, emotion, and thought are moving in the same direction. A verbal yes joined to bodily resistance and private resentment rarely lasts; inner alignment is the beginning of what can truly be carried. Before committing, take quiet time to write the cost you are willing to carry and the boundary you cannot accept; this reduces resentment created by an unwilling yes.
Remaining supple does not mean having no position. It means correcting your posture when facts change; in work and relationships, new information matters more than defending an outdated image. When revising a position, state which new fact changed your judgment. This builds more trust than pretending the earlier view never existed and makes updating a sign of competence.
After creating, do not rush to possess. Teach others, allow the work to be used, and let the result continue changing; ability then serves life instead of making life serve achievement and ownership. When releasing work, clarify its permitted use, attribution, and responsibility boundaries; the result can circulate without turning openness into a condition where nobody tends consequences.

en.title: The Usefulness Of Absence
verse: The thirty spokes unite in the one nave; but it is on the empty space (for the axle), that the use of the wheel depends.
Clay is fashioned into vessels; but it is on their empty hollowness, that their use depends.

Therefore, what has a (positive) existence serves for profitable adaptation, and what has not that for (actual) usefulness.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Judge a tool not only by what it contains but by the usable space it leaves. Meetings, rooms, and products work the same way; reducing crowding lets human attention and action enter. Observe where people pause, detour, or wait inside a space or process; these points of friction reveal the missing usable room more accurately than another feature list.
Relationships also depend on absence. Do not treat every silence as rejection or finish every sentence for the other person; unfilled space allows a genuine feeling to surface in its own time. During silence, remain present and agree when to return to the conversation. Neither interrogation nor disappearance is needed; safe space says the relationship remains while the answer forms.
With a complex problem, look for obstruction before adding more. One redundant process, vague responsibility, or demand that cannot be refused may be the true cause of failure; removal can help more than additional resources. Map the problem from beginning to end and mark repeated waiting, rework, and handoff confusion; removing one true obstruction can release the entire flow without adding resources.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Being stimulated is not the same as being nourished. After scrolling, purchasing, or joining excitement, notice whether you feel steadier or emptier; the body's after-effect is more reliable than the immediate rush. Record how a stimulus feels one hour later instead of trusting only immediate excitement; comparing these after-effects over time clarifies what nourishes and what merely numbs.
When choosing food, media, and relationships, ask less whether they look impressive and more whether they support your life. What helps you sleep, think clearly, and keep dignity deserves a lasting place in the day. Include effects on sleep, attention, money, and relationships in your selection criteria, so surface appeal cannot hide the cost that must be paid after something enters daily life.
Setting limits around the senses does not reject pleasure; it restores discernment. With less endless notification, comparison, and consumption, a simple meal, conversation, or period of attention can regain weight. Begin by disabling one unnecessary notification or protecting one screen-free period; as the senses recover, quieter forms of real satisfaction become perceptible again.

故贵为身于为天下，若可以托天下〔矣〕。

lineByLineTranslation: 受到宠爱或羞辱都像受惊一样，把大患看得像自身一样重要。
什么叫宠辱若惊？
受宠本来是居于下位；得到宠爱便惊喜，失去宠爱便惊恐，这就叫宠辱若惊。
什么叫把大患看得像自身一样重要？
我之所以有大患，是因为我执著于这个自身。
等到不再执著自身，还有什么祸患？
所以，能够像看重自身那样承担天下的人，才可以把天下托付给他。
能够爱惜自身并以此承担天下的人，才可以把天下交给他。

explanation.title: 本章主旨
explanation.body: 许多恐惧来自对身份、身体与得失的过度抓取。珍惜自己不等于围着自己旋转；当我们把个人安危放回更大的关系中，反而更能承担真正的责任。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
不要把一次得失扩大成“我这个人值不值得”。职位、关系和身体状态都会变化；把自我价值绑在它们上面，任何波动都会变成对身份的威胁。失去角色时，列出仍然存在的能力、关系和价值，提醒自己“发生了失败”不同于“我是失败的人”，恢复才有落脚点。
焦虑出现时，先辨认你真正要保护的是什么。很多控制并不是为了安全，而是害怕失去形象和确定感；说清核心需要，行动才不会被恐惧放大。把核心需要说成一句可以被回应的话，例如需要时间、信息或安全，而不是要求控制所有变量，行动会因此变得更准确。
珍惜自己，也要把自己放回关系之中。照顾身体、承认限度，同时不让个人安危成为所有决定的中心，才能既保护自己又承担对他人的责任。每个自我保护决定都检查对他人的外溢影响，并寻找较少转嫁成本的做法，自爱才能与共同责任同时成立。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 13
en.title: The Self And Its Burdens
verse: Favour and disgrace would seem equally to be feared; honour and great calamity, to be regarded as personal conditions (of the same kind).
What is meant by speaking thus of favour and disgrace?
Disgrace is being in a low position (after the enjoyment of favour).

The getting that (favour) leads to the apprehension (of losing it), and the losing it leads to the fear of (still greater calamity):--this is what is meant by saying that favour and disgrace would seem equally to be feared.
And what is meant by saying that honour and great calamity are to be (similarly) regarded as personal conditions?
What makes me liable to great calamity is my having the body (which I call myself); if I had not the body, what great calamity could come to me?

Therefore he who would administer the kingdom, honouring it as he honours his own person, may be employed to govern it, and he who would administer it with the love which he bears to his own person may be entrusted with it.

explanation.body: Beginning from “宠辱若惊，贵大患若身,” this chapter explores the self and its burdens. It does not demand a rigid answer; it asks how conditions, opposites, limits, and timing change what wise action looks like.

explanation.title: Chapter theme
explanation.body: Many fears grow from gripping identity, body, gain, and loss too tightly. Caring for ourselves need not mean revolving around ourselves; placing personal safety within a larger field of relationship can deepen responsibility.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not enlarge one gain or loss into a verdict on your worth. Roles, relationships, and bodily conditions all change; tying identity to them turns every fluctuation into a threat to the self. When a role is lost, list the capacities, relationships, and values that remain; distinguishing “a failure happened” from “I am a failure” gives recovery somewhere solid to begin.
When anxiety rises, identify what you are actually trying to protect. Much control serves not safety but fear of losing image or certainty; naming the core need keeps action from being magnified by fear. State the core need in a form another person can answer—time, information, or safety—rather than trying to control every variable; action then becomes more precise and proportionate.
Care for yourself while placing the self back inside relationship. Protect the body and acknowledge limits without making personal security the center of every decision; this supports both self-respect and responsibility to others. Review how each self-protective decision spills onto others and seek a way that transfers less cost; self-respect and shared responsibility can then remain true together.

sources.silkBTranscription: 視之而弗見，□之曰微；聽之而弗聞，命之曰希；德昏之而弗得，命之曰夷。三者不可至計，故混而為一。一者其上不謬，其下不忽。尋尋呵不可命也，復歸於無物。是胃無狀之狀，無物之象，是胃忽望。隋而不見其後，迎而不見其首。執今之道，以御今之有。以知古始，是胃道紀。
sources.receivedReference: 视之不见名曰夷，听之不闻名曰希，搏之不得名曰微。此三者不可致诘，故复混而为一。其上不皦，其下不昧，绳绳兮不可名，复归於无物。是谓无状之状，无象之象，无物之象，是谓惚恍。迎之不见其首，随之不见其后。执古之道，以御今之有，能知古始，是谓道纪。

zh.eyebrow: 帛书乙本底本校读 · 对应今本第十四章
zh.title: 视之而弗见，名之曰微
reconstructedVerse: 三者不可致诘，故混而为一。
一者，其上不曒，其下不昧。
绳绳不可名也，复归于无物。
是谓无状之状，无物之象，是谓忽恍。
随而不见其后，迎而不见其首。
执今之道，以御今之有，以知古始，是谓道纪。
lineByLineTranslation: 看它却看不见，给它取名叫作‘微’。
听它却听不到，给它取名叫作‘希’。
触摸它却得不到，给它取名叫作‘夷’。
这三者无法再追问到底，所以混合为一。
这个‘一’，上面不明亮，下面也不昏暗。
它绵延不绝而不可命名，又回到无物。
这叫没有形状的形状、没有物体的形象，也叫恍惚。
跟随它看不见末尾，迎着它也看不见开端。
把握今天的道，用来驾驭当下的事物，并由此认识古老的开端，这叫作道的纲纪。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 14
en.title: The Unnameable Whole
verse: We look at it, and we do not see it, and we name it 'the Equable.'
We listen to it, and we do not hear it, and we name it 'the Inaudible.'
We try to grasp it, and do not get hold of it, and we name it 'the Subtle.'
With these three qualities, it cannot be made the subject of description; and hence we blend them together and obtain The One.
Its upper part is not bright, and its lower part is not obscure.
Ceaseless in its action, it yet cannot be named, and then it again returns and becomes nothing.
This is called the Form of the Formless, and the Semblance of the Invisible; this is called the Fleeting and Indeterminable.
We meet it and do not see its Front; we follow it, and do not see its Back.
When we can lay hold of the Tao of old to direct the things of the present day, and are able to know it as it was of old in the beginning, this is called (unwinding) the clue of Tao.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
With a complex person, do not mistake a convenient explanation for understanding. History, body, environment, and what remains unsaid form a whole; admitting that you cannot see everything reduces the harm of certainty. Before judging a person, deliberately seek one piece of evidence that contradicts your first explanation; this interrupts the mind's habit of collecting only material that confirms bias.
In team problem-solving, decomposition is useful but relationships between parts still matter. Optimizing one metric can transfer pressure elsewhere; every improvement should be checked against the health of the whole. After changing one metric, also watch neighboring effects on quality, burden, and relationship; improvement in one place that creates damage everywhere else is not whole-system progress.
Allow an important matter to remain temporarily unnamed and unresolved. Not every feeling needs immediate classification; staying with an emerging question often reveals a direction more accurate than a fast definition. Set a date to revisit an unnamed question and record changes until then; patience is not indefinite delay, but a bounded period in which a more accurate form can emerge.

sources.silkBTranscription: 古之屳為道者，微眇玄達，深不可志。夫唯不可志，故強為之容，曰：與呵其若冬涉水，猷呵其若畏四𠳵，嚴呵其若客，浼呵其若淩澤，沌呵其若樸，湷呵其若濁，莊呵其若浴。濁而靜之，徐清。女以重之，徐生。葆此道□□欲盈。是以能敝而不成。
sources.receivedReference: 古之善为士者，微妙玄通，深不可识。夫惟不可识，故强为之容。豫若冬涉川，犹若畏四邻，俨若客，换若冰将释，敦兮其若朴，旷兮其若谷，浑兮其若浊。孰能浊以澄，静之徐清，孰能安以久，动之徐生。保此道者不欲盈。夫惟不盈，故能弊不新成。

zh.title: 古之善为道者，微妙玄达，
reconstructedVerse: 古之善为道者，微妙玄达，深不可识。
夫唯不可识，故强为之容。
曰：豫呵其若冬涉水，犹呵其若畏四邻，严呵其若客，涣呵其若凌释，敦呵其若朴，混呵其若浊，旷呵其若谷。
保此道〔不欲盈〕，〔夫唯不〕欲盈，是以能敝而不成。
lineByLineTranslation: 古时善于行道的人，精微、玄妙、通达，深得难以认识。
正因为难以认识，只能勉强描摹他们的样子。
他们谨慎啊，像冬天涉水；戒惧啊，像提防四邻；庄重啊，像作客；舒展啊，像冰将融化；敦厚啊，像未经雕琢的木；混融啊，像浑水；开阔啊，像山谷。
浑浊的水静下来，会慢慢澄清。
安静之中加以持守，生机便慢慢出现。
守住这条道而不求满盈；正因为不求满盈，所以能够承受损耗而不急于成全。

情绪混浊时，不急着发长消息或作永久承诺。先让身体慢下来，等激烈感受有了边界，再表达真正需要，通常能少说伤人的话、少做反复的决定。若必须回应，可以先发送一句“我需要冷静后再谈”，既不失联也不在激动中定案，为关系保留可修复的余地。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 15
en.title: Clarity Through Stillness
verse: The skilful masters (of the Tao) in old times, with a subtle and exquisite penetration, comprehended its mysteries, and were deep (also) so as to elude men's knowledge.
As they were thus beyond men's knowledge, I will make an effort to describe of what sort they appeared to be.

Shrinking looked they like those who wade through a stream in winter; irresolute like those who are afraid of all around them; grave like a guest (in awe of his host); evanescent like ice that is melting away; unpretentious like wood that has not been fashioned into anything; vacant like a valley, and dull like muddy water.
Who can (make) the muddy water (clear)?
Let it be still, and it will gradually become clear.
Who can secure the condition of rest?
Let movement go on, and the condition of rest will gradually arise.
They who preserve this method of the Tao do not wish to be full (of themselves).
It is through their not being full of themselves that they can afford to seem worn and not appear new and complete.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Reduce input before an important decision. Pause argument, messages, and new advice so the facts already present can settle overnight; many answers are hidden not by insufficient thought but by constant disturbance. Separate facts required for the decision from information that only increases anxiety, and stop searching once the evidence is sufficient; the mind then has room to weigh rather than accumulate.
When emotion is muddy, avoid sending the long message or making a permanent promise. Slow the body, let intensity find a boundary, and then name the real need; this prevents hurtful speech and repeated reversals. If a response is necessary, send “I need time to settle before we continue.” This preserves contact without making a permanent decision inside temporary intensity.
Stillness is not permanent inaction. Once clarity returns, take one necessary step and keep observing the result; silence used only for avoidance becomes another delay, while clear action completes the practice. Give the first clear step an observable result and review time; this prevents endless preparation while allowing feedback to revise action before everything is committed at once.

zh.title: 至虚极也，守静督也
reconstructedVerse: 万物旁作，吾以观其复也。
夫物芸芸，各复归于其〔根〕。
知常容，容乃公，公乃王，〔王乃〕天，天乃道，道乃〔久〕，没身不殆。
lineByLineTranslation: 把虚静推到极致，守住内在安静的准则。
万物一齐兴起，我从中观察它们的回归。
万物纷纭，各自回到自己的根。
回到根叫作静，静就叫作复归生命的本性。
复归本性是常，认识常道是明。
不认识常道，就会妄乱。
妄乱地行动，就会招来凶险。
认识常道便能包容；包容便能公正；公正便能成王；成王便合于天；天合于道；道因而长久，终身不会陷入危险。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 16
en.title: Return And Constancy
verse: The (state of) vacancy should be brought to the utmost degree, and that of stillness guarded with unwearying vigour.
All things alike go through their processes of activity, and (then) we see them return (to their original state).
When things (in the vegetable world) have displayed their luxuriant growth, we see each of them return to its root.
This returning to their root is what we call the state of stillness; and that stillness may be called a reporting that they have fulfilled their appointed end.
The report of that fulfilment is the regular, unchanging rule.
To know that unchanging rule is to be intelligent; not to know it leads to wild movements and evil issues.
The knowledge of that unchanging rule produces a (grand) capacity and forbearance, and that capacity and forbearance lead to a community (of feeling with all things).
From this community of feeling comes a kingliness of character; and he who is king-like goes on to be heaven-like.
In that likeness to heaven he possesses the Tao.
Possessed of the Tao, he endures long; and to the end of his bodily life, is exempt from all danger of decay.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not make a present peak into a permanent identity or a low point into a final verdict. Work, relationships, and emotion move in cycles; knowing they return reduces both arrogance and despair. Keep reserves during a peak and maintain basic rhythms during a low; this is practical respect for cycles and prevents temporary conditions from making permanent decisions.
A recurring problem often asks us to return to its root. Instead of treating the surface each time, examine sleep, boundaries, communication, and basic systems to find what keeps producing the same result. When the same problem appears three times, pause local repair and ask which environment or rule keeps producing it; identifying the repeating mechanism is how rework finally ends.
Review where you began at regular intervals. At the end of a quarter, relationship phase, or project, renew contact with the essential principle; a root you can return to keeps direction from moving with every wind. During review, record which principles still hold and which require renewal. A root is not loyalty to an old answer, but continued contact with what must not be lost.

explanation.body: 好的领导不必让所有人时刻感到被领导。说得少一点、控制少一点、把目标和边界说清楚，能让参与者真正拥有成果，而不是只会等待指令。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
好的带领先把目的和边界说清楚，而不是把每一步都替别人决定。团队知道为什么做、哪些不能碰，才有空间使用自己的判断，不必等指令才能行动。把边界写成少数可判断的原则，并允许成员在原则内选择路径；授权的尺度清楚，才不会在放手后又随时收回。
少说一点，把承诺留给实际支持。领导者反复强调权威，常说明系统缺少信任；稳定资源、及时承担责任，比持续展示存在感更能让人安心。遇到问题时先补资源、排除障碍、承担外部责任，再要求团队加速，这能分辨领导是在支持工作还是转移压力。
事情完成后，让参与者说“这是我们做成的”。分享决定权和功劳，不只是一种谦逊，也能培养下一位承担者，让成果不因领导者离开而消失。结束时邀请参与者说明他们学会了什么、下一次能独立承担什么，成果就从一次完成转化为可延续的共同能力。

In the next age they loved them and praised them.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Good leadership clarifies purpose and boundaries instead of deciding every step for others. When a team knows why the work matters and what must not be crossed, people can use judgment rather than waiting for instruction. Write boundaries as a few judgeable principles and let people choose methods within them; clear limits of authority prevent delegated power from being withdrawn whenever discomfort appears.
Speak less and let practical support carry the promise. Repeated displays of authority often reveal missing trust; stable resources and timely responsibility create more safety than constant visibility. When trouble arises, first add needed resources, remove obstacles, and carry external responsibility before asking the team to accelerate; this distinguishes support from pressure transfer.
After completion, let participants say, “We made this.” Shared decisions and credit are more than humility; they develop the next person who can carry the work when the current leader leaves. At completion, ask participants what they learned and what they can own next time; the result then becomes repeatable shared capacity rather than a single successful event.

related.body:
当一个组织不断增加口号和规章，先检查是不是信任已经受损。只要求人表现正确，可能把问题藏得更深；修复承诺、责任和公平，规则才不必无限加码。规则增加前先调查哪一次承诺被破坏、哪种不公平无人处理，修复源头往往比再发一份规范更能恢复秩序。
不要用“我这样做是为你好”代替真正的关系。善意需要接受对方的反馈，也要允许拒绝；不能被检验的好心，很容易变成控制或道德压力。善意行动前取得同意，并在过程中询问是否仍有帮助；能被拒绝和调整的关心，才真正把对方当成主体。

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
When an organization keeps adding slogans and rules, first ask whether trust has been damaged. Demanding correct appearances can drive the problem deeper; repairing promises, responsibility, and fairness reduces the need for endless regulation. Before adding rules, investigate which promise was broken and which unfairness remained unanswered; repairing that source often restores order better than publishing another policy.
Do not replace relationship with “I am doing this for your own good.” Care must receive feedback and allow refusal; goodwill that cannot be questioned easily becomes control or moral pressure. Seek consent before acting from goodwill and ask during the process whether the help still helps; care that can be refused and adjusted treats the recipient as a subject.
Values must hold in ordinary moments when no one is watching. Rather than declaring integrity or compassion, examine whether payments are timely, mistakes are owned, and vulnerable people are respected; conduct is closer to virtue than titles. Give values daily evidence through timeliness, transparency, respect, and accountability; when that evidence persists, an organization no longer needs loud declarations to prove its character.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Restate a complex problem in language an ordinary person can understand. If a team needs jargon to preserve a sense of expertise, it may have left the original need; clarity does not lower standards, it makes participation possible. Ask someone without background knowledge to restate your explanation; if they cannot name the purpose and next step, remove jargon until the information becomes genuinely usable.
Whenever adding a process, feature, or promise, name the concrete problem it solves. Complexity without a clear use continuously consumes attention; removing performative layers makes a system lighter and usable again. Every new layer of complexity needs an owner, maintenance cost, and exit condition; if these cannot be named, it may be adding burden rather than solving a problem.
Practice returning to simplicity in daily life as well. Buy one thing less, schedule one thing less, and prove one thing less; return time to food, sleep, care, and attention. Simplicity is not poverty but renewed contact with what matters. Choose one deliberate simplification each week and observe whether time returns to important life; simplicity matters when it deepens participation, not when it becomes another performance.

sources.silkBTranscription: 絕學無憂，唯與呵，其相去幾何？美與亞，其相去何若？人之所畏，亦不可以不畏人。朢呵其未央才！眾人熙熙。若鄉於大牢。而春登臺。我博焉未垗，若嬰兒未咳；纍呵佁無所歸。眾人皆又余，我愚人之心也，湷湷呵。鬻人昭昭，我獨若𨴽呵。鬻人察察，我獨閩閩呵，忽呵其若海，朢呵若無所止。眾人皆有以，我獨門元以鄙。吾欲獨異於人，而貴食母。
sources.receivedReference: 绝学无忧，唯之与阿，相去几何。善之与恶，相去何若。人之所畏，不可不畏。荒兮，其未央哉。众人熙熙，始享大牢，如登春台。我独怕兮，其未兆，如婴儿之未孩，乘乘兮，若无所归。众人皆有余，我独若遗，我愚人之心也哉。纯纯兮，俗人昭昭，我独若昏，俗人察察，我独闷闷。忽若晦，飂兮似无所止。众人皆有以，我独顽似鄙。我独异於人，而贵求食於母。

reconstructedVerse: 人之所畏，亦不可以不畏人。

lineByLineTranslation: 恭敬应答与呵斥，相距究竟有多远？

众人所畏惧的，也不能不有所畏惧。
辽远啊，这种差别还没有尽头！
众人兴高采烈，像享用盛宴，又像春日登台。

疲倦漂泊啊，像没有归宿。
众人都有余裕，只有我像有所匮乏。
我有一颗愚人的心，混沌啊。
世俗之人明明白白，只有我像昏暗。

浩荡啊，像大海。
飘忽啊，像没有停驻之处。
众人都有所凭借，只有我顽拙而鄙朴。

en.title: Different From The Crowd, Nourished By The Source
verse: When we renounce learning we have no troubles.
The (ready) 'yes,' and (flattering) 'yea;'-- Small is the difference they display.
But mark their issues, good and ill;-- What space the gulf between shall fill?
What all men fear is indeed to be feared; but how wide and without end is the range of questions (asking to be discussed)!
The multitude of men look satisfied and pleased; as if enjoying a full banquet, as if mounted on a tower in spring.
I alone seem listless and still, my desires having as yet given no indication of their presence.
I am like an infant which has not yet smiled.
I look dejected and forlorn, as if I had no home to go to.
The multitude of men all have enough and to spare.
I alone seem to have lost everything.
My mind is that of a stupid man; I am in a state of chaos.
Ordinary men look bright and intelligent, while I alone seem to be benighted.
They look full of discrimination, while I alone am dull and confused.
I seem to be carried about as on the sea, drifting as if I had nowhere to rest.
All men have their spheres of action, while I alone seem dull and incapable, like a rude borderer.
(Thus) I alone am different from other men, but I value the nursing-mother (the Tao).

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Being different from the majority does not require proving that you are more correct. First ask whether the choice makes life steadier and more honest; a difference sustained only by opposition is still being determined by others. Test a different path not by how unusual it looks, but by whether sleep, relationship, integrity, and long-term capacity improve; these are evidence of independent choice.
When loneliness appears, return to what genuinely nourishes you. Trusted friends, long reading, physical work, and quiet practice support an uncommon path more reliably than chasing recognition. Schedule regular time with a few trustworthy connections so loneliness does not drive emergency bids for approval from unsuitable groups; inner sources also need continuing nourishment.
Preserve the ability to remain connected with the group. Hold independent judgment while listening to other experience, and do not turn difference into superiority; a rooted person can be distinct without making everyone else an enemy. Keep one channel of dialogue open with people who disagree; independence then avoids becoming isolation, and a grounded position can understand another view before choosing again.

explanation.title: 本章主旨
explanation.body: 方向比一时的技巧更重要。面对诱惑和噪声，反复确认什么让生命更真实、更少强迫，再把小决定向那个方向对齐，道路会在行走中逐渐清楚。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
先确定方向，再挑选方法。工具、课程和技巧不断更新，如果不知道自己要保护什么，它们只会制造新的忙碌；方向清楚，简单的方法也能持续积累。写下未来一年最想保护的三件事，再用它们筛选工具与机会；不能服务方向的“先进”，也可以放心不追。
面对诱惑时，问它会把你带向哪里，而不只问现在是否舒服。一次决定看起来很小，但重复的消费、表达和承诺会共同塑造道路。把小决定放进半年后的连续结果里想象，能看见重复会形成怎样的生活，短暂诱惑便不再只是孤立的一次。
道路不必一开始就完全看清。让每一步与真实、少强迫、可持续对齐，再根据反馈调整；方向可以坚定，路线仍然保持开放。每走一段就检查是否更真实、更少强迫、更可持续；路线调整应回应反馈，而不是因为别人走得更快就慌乱换道。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 21
en.title: Follow The Way
verse: The grandest forms of active force From Tao come, their only source.
Who can of Tao the nature tell?
Our sight it flies, our touch as well.
Eluding sight, eluding touch, The forms of things all in it crouch; Eluding touch, eluding sight, There are their semblances, all right.
Profound it is, dark and obscure; Things' essences all there endure.
Those essences the truth enfold Of what, when seen, shall then be told.
Now it is so; 'twas so of old.
Its name--what passes not away; So, in their beautiful array, Things form and never know decay.
How know I that it is so with all the beauties of existing things?
By this (nature of the Tao).

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Choose direction before choosing technique. Tools, courses, and methods keep changing; without knowing what must be protected, they create new busyness. A clear direction lets even simple practices accumulate. Write the three things you most want to protect over the next year, then use them to filter tools and opportunities; what cannot serve direction need not be chased.
When temptation appears, ask where it will take you rather than only whether it feels good now. A single choice looks small, but repeated purchases, words, and commitments gradually form a road. Imagine a small decision repeated for six months and notice the life it constructs; the immediate temptation is then visible as part of a path, not an isolated act.
The whole path does not need to be visible at the beginning. Align each step with truth, less coercion, and sustainability, then adjust from feedback; direction can remain firm while the route stays open. At intervals, ask whether the path is becoming more honest, less forced, and more sustainable; revise from feedback rather than changing course because someone else moves faster.

related.title: 对我们的启发

把注意力从“别人怎么看我”移回事情本身。展示成绩、争抢功劳会让人持续维护形象；专注解决真实问题，能力才能变成结果而不是表演。在汇报前先写“这件事为谁解决了什么”，若答案不清楚，就继续做事而不是先包装成绩，注意力会自然回到价值。
做得好时，不必贬低别人来证明自己。说明贡献也承认条件和协作，能让成功更可信，并减少团队因比较产生的防御和内耗。庆祝成功时列出条件、运气和协作，不是削弱贡献，而是让团队知道哪些因素值得保留、哪些结果不能简单复制。
发现自己急着解释、炫耀或证明时，先停下来问：我害怕别人误会什么？照顾那份不安，比继续放大声音更能恢复内在稳定。当不安出现，先向可信的人确认具体事实，而不是向所有人扩音；得到准确反馈后，再决定是否真的需要解释。

en.title: Do Not Display Or Boast
verse: He who stands on his tiptoes does not stand firm; he who stretches his legs does not walk (easily).

(So), he who displays himself does not shine; he who asserts his own views is not distinguished; he who vaunts himself does not find his merit acknowledged; he who is self-conceited has no superiority allowed to him.
Such conditions, viewed from the standpoint of the Tao, are like remnants of food, or a tumour on the body, which all dislike.
Hence those who pursue (the course) of the Tao do not adopt and allow them.
