related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Move attention from how others see you back to the work itself. Display and competition for credit require continuous image maintenance; solving the real problem turns ability into a result rather than a performance. Before reporting, write who the work helped and what it solved; if the answer is unclear, continue improving the work rather than packaging achievement prematurely.
When you do well, there is no need to diminish another person. Name your contribution while acknowledging conditions and collaboration; this makes success more credible and reduces defensive comparison inside a team. When celebrating, name conditions, luck, and collaboration alongside contribution; this does not diminish success, but shows the team what can be preserved and what cannot simply be repeated.
When you feel compelled to explain, display, or prove, pause and ask what misunderstanding you fear. Caring for that insecurity restores inner stability more effectively than increasing the volume. When insecurity rises, seek specific facts from one trustworthy person rather than broadcasting more loudly; after accurate feedback, decide whether any explanation is actually needed.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
遇到阻力时，调整姿势不等于认输。换时间、换表达、先退一步，都可能保存真正要守护的东西；僵硬坚持一种形式，反而容易把核心一起折断。调整前明确自己真正守护的是关系、质量还是安全，核心说得越清楚，形式改变时越不容易误以为自己背叛了原则。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 22
en.title: Yielding Preserves Wholeness
verse: The partial becomes complete; the crooked, straight; the empty, full; the worn out, new.
He whose (desires) are few gets them; he whose (desires) are many goes astray.
Therefore the sage holds in his embrace the one thing (of humility), and manifests it to all the world.

He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; from self-assertion, and therefore he is distinguished; from self-boasting, and therefore his merit is acknowledged; from self-complacency, and therefore he acquires superiority.
It is because he is thus free from striving that therefore no one in the world is able to strive with him.
That saying of the ancients that 'the partial becomes complete' was not vainly spoken:--all real completion is comprehended under it.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Adjusting your posture under resistance is not surrender. Changing timing, wording, or taking one step back may preserve what truly matters; rigid loyalty to one form can break the core along with it. Before adapting, name whether you are protecting relationship, quality, or safety; the clearer the core, the less a change of form feels like betrayal of principle.
In relationship, allow yourself to lower defense first. Hearing the other person, acknowledging part of the truth, or correcting one sentence does not erase your position; flexibility can return the relationship to conversation. Begin by acknowledging one part the other person has right, then state your boundary; this does not trade positions, but creates a step back into shared facts.
When reality changes a plan, separate principles that must remain from methods that can be remade. Distinguishing core from form prevents both easy abandonment and the prideful continuation of a mistake. When remaking a plan, mark what must remain and what can be tested; bounded adaptation avoids both total collapse and the worship of an obsolete method.

zh.title: 希言自然
reconstructedVerse: 飘风不终朝，暴雨不终日。
天地而弗能久，又况于人乎！
故从事而道者同于道，德者同于德，失者同于失。
lineByLineTranslation: 少说话，才合乎自然。
狂风刮不了一早晨，暴雨下不了一整天。
是谁造成这些？
天地尚且不能让猛烈状态持久，何况人呢？
所以从事于道的人与道相同，从事于德的人与德相同，走向失落的人也与失落相同。
与德相同的人，道也以德回应他。
与失落相同的人，道也让他承受失落。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 23
en.title: Few Words And Naturalness
verse: Abstaining from speech marks him who is obeying the spontaneity of his nature.
A violent wind does not last for a whole morning; a sudden rain does not last for the whole day.
To whom is it that these (two) things are owing?
To Heaven and Earth.
If Heaven and Earth cannot make such (spasmodic) actings last long, how much less can man!

Therefore when one is making the Tao his business, those who are also pursuing it, agree with him in it, and those who are making the manifestation of its course their object agree with him in that; while even those who are failing in both these things agree with him where they fail.

Hence, those with whom he agrees as to the Tao have the happiness of attaining to it; those with whom he agrees as to its manifestation have the happiness of attaining to it; and those with whom he agrees in their failure have also the happiness of attaining (to the Tao).
(But) when there is not faith sufficient (on his part), a want of faith (in him) ensues (on the part of the others).

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Not every pause needs immediate speech. In meetings, conflict, and companionship, waiting a few seconds lets the real question appear and prevents habitual language from covering what is not yet understood. During the pause, notice what you want to avoid or prove too quickly; these seconds are not a communication trick but room for unformed truth to enter language.
Promise less and complete what you say. Constant declarations dilute the weight of language; when action, time, and results testify for you, trust can grow from stable experience. Keep a promise list and regularly remove commitments you cannot honor; fewer completed words gradually regain weight and give others a reliable basis for trust.
When communicating something important, remove exaggeration and unnecessary defense. State the fact, the need, and the next step; words close to reality need less volume and repetition to hold. Before sending, ask whether each sentence adds evidence or necessary context; remove paragraphs that only repeat position so the other person can respond to clearer information.

verse: There was something undefined and complete, coming into existence before Heaven and Earth.
How still it was and formless, standing alone, and undergoing no change, reaching everywhere and in no danger (of being exhausted)!
It may be regarded as the Mother of all things.
I do not know its name, and I give it the designation of the Tao (the Way or Course).
Making an effort (further) to give it a name I call it The Great.
Great, it passes on (in constant flow).
Passing on, it becomes remote.
Having become remote, it returns.
Therefore the Tao is great; Heaven is great; Earth is great; and the (sage) king is also great.
In the universe there are four that are great, and the (sage) king is one of them.
Man takes his law from the Earth; the Earth takes its law from Heaven; Heaven takes its law from the Tao.
The law of the Tao is its being what it is.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Understand a thing's own conditions before acting. Plants, teams, relationships, and bodies all have timing; a reasonable goal does not mean every moment and method can produce the same result. Before beginning, observe whether resources, relational readiness, and bodily capacity are present; when conditions are missing, cultivate the environment instead of using willpower to make a reasonable goal harmful.
When progress is slow, do not assume that willpower is missing. Resources, trust, or capacity may not yet be mature; supplying conditions works more deeply than continued pressure. Give slow progress stage indicators and identify whether practice, trust, or support is missing; once the lack is specific, pressure can be replaced by assistance that actually helps.
Respect for what is natural is not neglect. Water what needs water, set the necessary boundary, and then stop unnecessary manipulation; tend the requirements of growth without prescribing every posture of life. After tending the conditions, agree on a period without intervention and observe real feedback; if every new growth is rearranged, life can never reveal its own direction.

en.title: Gravity And Stillness As Roots
verse: Gravity is the root of lightness; stillness, the ruler of movement.
Therefore a wise prince, marching the whole day, does not go far from his baggage waggons.
Although he may have brilliant prospects to look at, he quietly remains (in his proper place), indifferent to them.
How should the lord of a myriad chariots carry himself lightly before the kingdom?
If he do act lightly, he has lost his root (of gravity); if he proceed to active movement, he will lose his throne.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Steady the body before making an important decision. Slow the breath, sit firmly, and confirm basic facts; this returns you from agitation to a center. Speed without a root often reaches the wrong place sooner. Create a bodily reset before major decisions—walk for ten minutes, eat, and verify the data—so excitement or panic cannot disguise speed as clarity.
Do not allow every new message to reorder priorities. Teams and lives need a few stable principles; finish what truly matters before following the surrounding excitement. Let only genuinely new facts change the day's priorities; volume and urgency do not automatically move forward in line, allowing stable principles to create a predictable rhythm.
Carry weight without becoming heavy and rigid. Stability does not reject change; it preserves a rhythm, boundary, and value to return to, so movement still has direction. Methods may be revised regularly while rest, review, and core boundaries stay dependable; these return points keep flexibility from becoming directionless reaction.

故善人，善人之师，不善人，善人之资也。
不贵其师，不爱其资，唯智乎大迷，是谓妙要。

也不抛弃任何材料，这叫作内藏的明智。
所以善人是不善者的老师，不善者是善人可以借鉴的材料。
不尊重老师，也不爱惜可以借鉴的材料，即使自以为聪明也会陷入大迷惑，这叫作精妙的要领。

en.title: Save Without Discarding
verse: The skilful traveller leaves no traces of his wheels or footsteps; the skilful speaker says nothing that can be found fault with or blamed; the skilful reckoner uses no tallies; the skilful closer needs no bolts or bars, while to open what he has shut will be impossible; the skilful binder uses no strings or knots, while to unloose what he has bound will be impossible.
In the same way the sage is always skilful at saving men, and so he does not cast away any man; he is always skilful at saving things, and so he does not cast away anything.
This is called 'Hiding the light of his procedure.'
Therefore the man of skill is a master (to be looked up to) by him who has not the skill; and he who has not the skill is the helper of (the reputation of) him who has the skill.
If the one did not honour his master, and the other did not rejoice in his helper, an (observer), though intelligent, might greatly err about them.
This is called 'The utmost degree of mystery.'

When addressing an error, the goal is not to prove who is worst but to restore a working system. Protect those affected while giving the person responsible a clear duty and path to repair. A repair path needs an account of impact, specific responsibility, supporting resources, and a later review—not punishment alone—so the system can actually learn from error.
When resources are limited, do not care only for the most visible part. Neglected people, materials, and details may hold future possibility; preservation and reuse reduce the long cost of exclusion. During resource review, list what is unused but repairable; recombination saves cost and often reveals value that the previous evaluation system failed to recognize.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
知道自己有力量，也要保留接纳和倾听。能力若只能通过控制表现，就会把周围的人变得被动；能承接反馈，力量才不必靠压住别人来成立。掌握力量时安排固定的反馈入口，并让不同意见不会遭到惩罚；能被现实纠正的能力，才不必靠不断加压证明自己。
不要只发展被赞美的一面。果断的人也需要柔软，善良的人也需要边界；允许两端共同存在，性格才不会因为长期压抑而突然反弹。每周观察自己长期隐藏的是哪一端，并做一次安全的小练习，例如坚定者请求帮助、温和者清楚拒绝，让人格重新取得平衡。
在竞争环境里，守住不争先的空间。先观察、先让别人表达、先看整体需要，并不减少影响力；真正成熟的领导常从容纳开始。让别人先说并不等于永远退后；听见全局后再在关键处承担，影响力会更准确，也更少制造被迫服从。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 28
en.title: Know Strength, Keep Receptivity
verse: Who knows his manhood's strength, Yet still his female feebleness maintains; As to one channel flow the many drains, All come to him, yea, all beneath the sky.
Thus he the constant excellence retains; The simple child again, free from all stains.

Who knows how white attracts, Yet always keeps himself within black's shade, The pattern of humility displayed, Displayed in view of all beneath the sky; He in the unchanging excellence arrayed, Endless return to man's first state has made.
Who knows how glory shines, Yet loves disgrace, nor e'er for it is pale; Behold his presence in a spacious vale, To which men come from all beneath the sky.
The unchanging excellence completes its tale; The simple infant man in him we hail.
The unwrought material, when divided and distributed, forms vessels.
The sage, when employed, becomes the Head of all the Officers (of government); and in his greatest regulations he employs no violent measures.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Know your strength while preserving receptivity and listening. Ability expressed only through control makes others passive; receiving feedback lets power exist without pressing everyone else down. When holding power, create a regular path for feedback and protect disagreement from punishment; capacity that reality can correct does not need constant pressure to prove itself.
Do not develop only the side that receives praise. Decisive people need softness and kind people need boundaries; allowing both poles prevents a suppressed quality from returning in destructive form. Notice which side of yourself has been hidden, then practice its safe opposite once: the decisive person requests help, or the gentle person gives a clear refusal.
In a competitive setting, protect some space from the need to be first. Observe, let others speak, and notice the whole need; mature influence often begins with the capacity to contain. Letting others speak first does not mean permanent retreat; after hearing the whole, assume responsibility at the necessary point so influence becomes more accurate and less coercive.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
不要把一个复杂系统当成可以任意摆弄的物件。家庭、组织和环境都有自发秩序；大规模改变前，先了解连锁影响，避免解决一处却破坏更多地方。重大改变前画出受影响的人、资源和后续环节，并从最脆弱处做小规模试验；看见连锁反应后再扩大，代价会小得多。
能干预，不等于都该干预。看到别人作出与你不同的选择时，分清这是伤害、共同责任，还是只让你不舒服；不属于你的部分要学会停手。当你想介入时先写下若不行动会发生什么，若只是结果不合偏好而没有伤害，就把不适留给自己消化。
管理的重点是照看条件和底线，而不是控制每个动作。规则清楚、信息透明、反馈可达，人往往比被频繁纠正时更能形成稳定秩序。好的治理还要让反馈能安全返回决策者，并约定何时重新评估规则；条件被照看，控制才可能真正减少。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 29
en.title: The World Cannot Be Forced
verse: If any one should wish to get the kingdom for himself, and to effect this by what he does, I see that he will not succeed.
The kingdom is a spirit-like thing, and cannot be got by active doing.
He who would so win it destroys it; he who would hold it in his grasp loses it.
The course and nature of things is such that What was in front is now behind; What warmed anon we freezing find.
Strength is of weakness oft the spoil; The store in ruins mocks our toil.
Hence the sage puts away excessive effort, extravagance, and easy indulgence.

explanation.title: Plain reading · Read the movement of the whole chapter
explanation.body: Beginning from “将欲取天下而为之，吾见其,” this chapter explores the world cannot be forced. It does not demand a rigid answer; it asks how conditions, opposites, limits, and timing change what wise action looks like.

explanation.title: Chapter theme
explanation.body: The world is not an object to manipulate at will; total control easily damages spontaneous order. Our task is to tend conditions, reduce harm, and stop intervening where the work is not ours.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Do not treat a complex system as an object that can be manipulated at will. Families, organizations, and environments have spontaneous order; before a large intervention, examine the chain of effects. Before major change, map affected people, resources, and downstream links, then test at the most vulnerable point on a small scale; expand only after the chain of effects is visible.
The ability to intervene does not mean every intervention is yours. When someone chooses differently, distinguish harm and shared responsibility from mere discomfort; learn to stop where the work is not yours. Before intervening, write what would happen if you did nothing; when the outcome merely differs from preference and causes no harm, carry your discomfort instead of controlling others.
Management should tend conditions and essential boundaries rather than control every motion. Clear rules, transparent information, and reachable feedback create steadier order than constant correction. Good governance also lets feedback return safely to decision-makers and sets a date to review rules; when conditions are tended, control can genuinely decrease.

sources.silkBTranscription: 以道佐人主，不以兵強於天下。其□□□□□□□□棘生之。善者果而已矣，毌以取強焉。果而毌驕，果而勿矜，果□□傷，果而毌得已居。是胃果而強。物壯而老，胃之不道。不道蚤已。
sources.receivedReference: 以道佐人主者，不以兵强天下。其事好还，师之所处，荆棘生焉。大军之后，必有凶年。故善者果而已，不敢以取强。果而勿矜，果而勿伐，果而勿骄，果而不得已，果而勿强。物壮则老，是谓不道，不道早已。

zh.eyebrow: 帛书乙本底本校读 · 对应今本第三十章
zh.title: 以道佐人主，不以兵强于天
reconstructedVerse: 以道佐人主，不以兵强于天下，其〔事好还〕。
善者果而已矣，毋以取强焉。
果而毋骄，果而毋矜，果〔而毋〕伐，果而毋得已居，是谓果而〔不〕强。
物壮而老，〔是〕谓之不道，不道早已。
lineByLineTranslation: 用道辅佐君主的人，不凭武力在天下逞强，因为这种事很容易反噬。
军队驻扎过的地方，荆棘丛生。
善于用兵的人达到目的便停止，不借此求强。
达到目的却不骄傲、不自高、不夸耀；只在不得已时达到目的，这叫达到目的而不逞强。
事物强壮以后便会衰老，这叫不合于道；不合于道就会早早终止。

explanation.title: 本章主旨
explanation.body: 达成目标与压服别人不是同一回事。事情做成之后，不夸耀、不逼迫、不把偶然胜利变成永久资格，才能避免成果继续制造新的冲突。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
达到目标后，不要把成功变成压服别人的资格。一次有效的方法未必适合所有人；保留谦逊，能防止成果继续制造新的反抗和冲突。成功后重新询问使用者和受影响者，而不是只复制原方法；成果若不能容纳新条件，很快会从经验变成压迫。
推动事情时，给对方理解、回应和选择的空间。只靠压力得到的配合，在压力消失后也容易消失；共同认可的方向才更可能持续。给对方一个可拒绝、可修改的参与方式，并说明不同选择的真实后果，自主形成的承诺才有机会穿过困难。
复盘时除了问“做成没有”，也问用了什么代价。若结果建立在恐惧、羞辱或长期透支上，就需要重新设计方法，而不是只庆祝数字。把隐性代价换算成离职、返工、健康和信任损失，数字之外的损耗被看见，复盘才足以指导下一次设计。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 30
en.title: Accomplish Without Coercion
verse: He who would assist a lord of men in harmony with the Tao will not assert his mastery in the kingdom by force of arms.
Such a course is sure to meet with its proper return.
Wherever a host is stationed, briars and thorns spring up.
In the sequence of great armies there are sure to be bad years.
A skilful (commander) strikes a decisive blow, and stops.
He does not dare (by continuing his operations) to assert and complete his mastery.
He will strike the blow, but will be on his guard against being vain or boastful or arrogant in consequence of it.
He strikes it as a matter of necessity; he strikes it, but not from a wish for mastery.
When things have attained their strong maturity they become old.
This may be said to be not in accordance with the Tao: and what is not in accordance with it soon comes to an end.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
After reaching a goal, do not turn success into a license to overpower others. One effective method may not fit everyone; humility prevents an achievement from creating the next resistance and conflict. After success, ask users and affected people again instead of simply repeating the method; an achievement that cannot hold new conditions soon turns from experience into oppression.
When moving work forward, leave room for understanding, response, and choice. Cooperation produced only by pressure often disappears when pressure does; a direction people can recognize together lasts longer. Offer a way to refuse or modify participation and explain the real consequences of each choice; commitment formed with agency has a better chance of surviving difficulty.
In review, ask not only whether the result was achieved but what it cost. If success depends on fear, humiliation, or chronic exhaustion, redesign the method instead of celebrating the number alone. Translate hidden cost into turnover, rework, health, and lost trust; once damage beyond the headline number is visible, review can genuinely guide the next design.

sources.silkBTranscription: 夫兵者，不祥之器也，物或亞□□□□□□□。□子居則貴左，用兵則貴右。故兵者非君子之器；兵者不祥□器也，不得已而用之，銛龍為上，勿美也。若美之，是樂殺人也。夫樂殺人，不可以得志於天下矣。是以吉事□□□□□□，是以偏將軍居左，而上將軍居右，言以喪禮居之也。殺□□□□□立□□朕而以喪禮處之。
sources.receivedReference: 夫佳兵者，不祥之器。物或恶之，故有道者不处。君子居则贵左，用兵则贵右。兵者，不祥之器，非君子之器，不得已而用之。恬憺为上。胜而不美，而美之者，是乐杀人。夫乐杀人者，不可以得志於天下矣。故吉事尚左，凶事尚右，偏将军处左，上将军处右。言以丧礼处之。杀人众多，以悲哀泣之。战胜，以丧礼处之。

zh.eyebrow: 帛书乙本底本校读 · 对应今本第三十一章
zh.title: 夫兵者，不祥之器也
reconstructedVerse: 物或恶〔之〕，〔故有欲者弗居〕。
〔君〕子居则贵左，用兵则贵右，故兵者非君子之器〔也〕。
兵者不祥〔之〕器也，不得已而用之，铦袭为上，勿美也。
夫乐杀人，不可以得志于天下矣。
是以吉事〔上左〕，〔丧事上右〕。
是以偏将军居左，上将军居右。
lineByLineTranslation: 兵器是不吉祥的器物。
万物或许都厌恶它，所以有所欲求的人不愿居于其中。
君子平时以左为贵，用兵时却以右为贵，所以兵器不是君子的器物。
兵器是不祥之器，只在不得已时使用；锋芒收敛才是上策，不要赞美它。
如果赞美战争，就是以杀人为乐。
以杀人为乐的人，不可能在天下实现自己的志向。
所以吉庆之事以左边为上，丧事以右边为上。
因此偏将军居左，上将军居右。
这就是说要以丧礼的态度对待战争。
杀人众多，应当怀着悲痛哀悼的心面对。
即使战胜，也要按丧礼来处理。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 31
en.title: Weapons Are Inauspicious
verse: Now arms, however beautiful, are instruments of evil omen, hateful, it may be said, to all creatures.
Therefore they who have the Tao do not like to employ them.
The superior man ordinarily considers the left hand the most honourable place, but in time of war the right hand.
Those sharp weapons are instruments of evil omen, and not the instruments of the superior man;--he uses them only on the compulsion of necessity.
Calm and repose are what he prizes; victory (by force of arms) is to him undesirable.
To consider this desirable would be to delight in the slaughter of men; and he who delights in the slaughter of men cannot get his will in the kingdom.
On occasions of festivity to be on the left hand is the prized position; on occasions of mourning, the right hand.
The second in command of the army has his place on the left; the general commanding in chief has his on the right;--his place, that is, is assigned to him as in the rites of mourning.
He who has killed multitudes of men should weep for them with the bitterest grief; and the victor in battle has his place (rightly) according to those rites.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Keep coercion as a last resort rather than choosing it first because it acts quickly. Power, punishment, and threat leave a long memory; matters that can be resolved through explanation, negotiation, and repair need not begin with harm. Before punishment, record which explanation, negotiation, and repair attempts were made and why they were insufficient; this order keeps convenient power from becoming the first response.
Even when conflict must be stopped, do not take pleasure in victory. Acknowledge losses, care for innocent impact, and leave a path back to relationship so justice does not become numbness. After stopping harm, distinguish what responsible people, affected people, and witnesses each need; care beyond victory prevents fear from continuing to spread through the group.
After an intense event, give a team time for recovery instead of forcing an immediate return to normal. Reviewing facts, naming fear, and rebuilding safety prevents unspoken harm from continuing through the system. Recovery needs safe expression, structural correction, and later review; emotional release without changed conditions leaves the injury ready to return in another form.

lineByLineTranslation: 道恒常无名，未经雕琢的朴虽然微小，天下却没有谁敢使它臣服。
侯王若能守住它，万物会自然归顺。
天地之气相合，降下甘露，没有人命令，甘露也会自然均匀。
制度开始便有名称；名称既已产生，也应当知道适可而止，知道停止才不会危险。
道存在于天下，就像小溪山谷最终汇入江海。

en.eyebrow: Silk B Base Reading · Received Chapter 32
en.title: Simplicity And Knowing When To Stop
verse: The Tao, considered as unchanging, has no name.
Though in its primordial simplicity it may be small, the whole world dares not deal with (one embodying) it as a minister.
If a feudal prince or the king could guard and hold it, all would spontaneously submit themselves to him.
Heaven and Earth (under its guidance) unite together and send down the sweet dew, which, without the directions of men, reaches equally everywhere as of its own accord.
As soon as it proceeds to action, it has a name.
When it once has that name, (men) can know to rest in it.
When they know to rest in it, they can be free from all risk of failure and error.
The relation of the Tao to all the world is like that of the great rivers and seas to the streams from the valleys.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Institutions and tools must serve the purpose rather than forcing the purpose to serve them. As process grows, regularly ask whether it still solves a real problem; rules without a use should be simplified or stopped. Give processes an expiration date and remove them unless someone can show continuing value; institutions should prove their usefulness rather than demand permanent adaptation from people.
Knowing what is enough protects the boundary of power. Do not expand authority after the duty is complete or hoard resources after needs are met; otherwise the wish to do well becomes endless control. State where a responsibility ends and require new authorization beyond it; when power stops at the task boundary, good intentions are less likely to expand without limit.
In complexity, return to plain questions: who is affected, what are the facts, where is the boundary, and who owns the next step? A simple frame often moves work farther than an impressive concept. Turn the four simple questions into records: reachable affected people, verifiable facts, explainable boundaries, and an owner with a deadline; complexity then begins to move.

zh.title: 知人者，智也
lineByLineTranslation: 了解别人，是有智慧。
了解自己，才是明白。
战胜别人，是有力量。
战胜自己，才是真正强大。
知道满足，就是富有。

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
认识别人只能提供信息，认识自己才决定如何回应。被批评、被诱惑或被催促时，先辨认自己的害怕和需要，别让外部声音直接接管行动。在被触发时先给情绪命名，再问它提醒了什么边界或需要；能说出内在发生什么，外部声音就不必直接决定行为。
胜过自己不是压住感受，而是不让冲动掌舵。愤怒可以提供边界信息，欲望可以显示渴望；听见它们，再由更长远的价值决定下一步。为冲动设置一个不会造成伤害的出口，例如写下、运动或延迟回应，让感受完成表达，同时把方向交给长期价值。
建立一份诚实的自我记录。定期写下什么让你有生命力、什么反复消耗、哪些承诺并非真心愿意；自知来自长期观察，不来自一句性格标签。记录之后每月寻找重复模式，并选择一个最小调整；自知若不能改变一点生活，很容易只变成更精致的自我描述。

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Knowing other people provides information; knowing yourself determines the response. When criticized, tempted, or hurried, identify your own fear and need before outside voices take direct control of action. When triggered, name the emotion and ask which boundary or need it signals; describing the inner event keeps an outside voice from directly deciding behavior.
Mastering yourself does not mean suppressing feeling. Anger can reveal a boundary and desire can reveal a longing; hear the information, then let a longer value choose the next step. Give impulse a harmless outlet—write, move, or delay the response—so feeling can be expressed while long-term values retain authority over direction.
Keep an honest record of the self. Regularly note what gives you life, what repeatedly drains you, and which promises were never a genuine yes; self-knowledge grows through observation, not one personality label. Review the record monthly for repeating patterns and choose one small adjustment; self-knowledge that changes no part of life easily becomes only a refined description.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
真正重要的工作，不必一直把自己放在中心。把注意力投向问题、使用者和共同目标，个人声量变小，成果的实际影响反而可能更大。承担任务时约定成果标准与反馈方式，然后减少不必要的自我呈现；中心留给问题，个人反而更容易得到准确评价。
拥有位置时，主动让别人被看见。邀请不同意见、分享资源、把机会给尚未有舞台的人，能让影响力从个人扩大为共同能力。分享机会要包含准备支持和真实决策权，否则让人“被看见”仍可能只是装饰，并没有形成新的共同能力。
不要用“我不重要”假装谦逊。清楚承担自己的责任，也不夸大独特性；既不自轻也不自大，才能稳定服务比自己更大的事情。检验谦逊可以看你是否既能接受感谢，也能承认错误；不逃避自己的分量，才能稳定地把力量用于共同目标。

en.title: Greatness Without Self-Importance
verse: All-pervading is the Great Tao!
It may be found on the left hand and on the right.
All things depend on it for their production, which it gives to them, not one refusing obedience to it.
When its work is accomplished, it does not claim the name of having done it.
It clothes all things as with a garment, and makes no assumption of being their lord;--it may be named in the smallest things.
All things return (to their root and disappear), and do not know that it is it which presides over their doing so;--it may be named in the greatest things.
Hence the sage is able (in the same way) to accomplish his great achievements.
It is through his not making himself great that he can accomplish them.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Work that truly matters does not require keeping the self at the center. Direct attention to the problem, the people served, and the shared aim; a quieter personal image can produce greater practical impact. When owning a task, agree on outcome standards and feedback, then reduce unnecessary self-presentation; leaving the center to the problem often produces more accurate recognition.
When you hold a position, deliberately make others visible. Invite dissent, share resources, and give opportunity to people without a stage; influence then grows from one person into common capacity. Sharing opportunity must include preparation and real decision authority; visibility without power can remain decorative and does not create new collective capacity.
Do not disguise self-erasure as humility. Carry your responsibility clearly without exaggerating uniqueness; neither diminishing nor enlarging yourself allows stable service to something larger. Test humility by whether you can receive gratitude and admit error; not escaping your actual weight is what makes strength reliably available to a shared purpose.

en.title: Hold The Great Image
verse: To him who holds in his hands the Great Image (of the invisible Tao), the whole world repairs.
Men resort to him, and receive no hurt, but (find) rest, peace, and the feeling of ease.
Music and dainties will make the passing guest stop (for a time).
But though the Tao as it comes from the mouth, seems insipid and has no flavour, though it seems not worth being looked at or listened to, the use of it is inexhaustible.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
A shared vision cannot remain a pleasing slogan. Translate it into concrete arrangements for safety, dignity, time, and resources so people can see how the direction improves real life. Translate vision into changes observable within three months and publish who owns them and who receives support; ideals become shared reality only after entering time and resources.
Invite people toward a purpose rather than using greatness to force obedience. Explain why it matters while allowing questions and different speeds; voluntary participation is stronger than passive uniformity. Explain levels of participation and a way to leave, so people can approach according to capacity; a voluntary community preserves genuine contribution better than visible compliance.
A vision must survive ordinary testing. Regularly examine whether policies, products, and collaboration still serve the original promise; if effects contradict it, change the practice rather than defending the slogan. Regularly ask the most affected people to describe actual experience; when it contradicts the slogan, change the system first, because credible vision accepts correction by reality.

related.title: 对我们的启发
related.body:
遇到坚硬的人或制度，先找可以进入的缝隙。一次准确的问题、一个可接受的小改变，常比正面证明谁更强更能推动长期变化。面对僵局先寻找双方都能接受的最小改变，并约定用结果决定下一步；小入口能降低防御，也让变化获得真实证据。
柔软不等于没有边界。语气可以温和，原则仍可清楚；把对抗降下来，让对方有机会听见内容，比同时提高声量更有作用，也更容易留下合作空间。表达边界时说清具体行为、影响和后果，不把人整体否定；柔和语气配上明确结构，原则才不会被误解为请求。
把改变做成持续作用，而不是一次爆发。稳定反馈、反复示范和小步修正看起来慢，却能穿过防御，使新习惯真正留在系统里。若目标确实重要，就接受它可能需要多轮微调而非一次征服；耐心保存了后续合作所需的人与信任。

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
With a rigid person or institution, look first for an opening. One precise question or acceptable small change often moves long-term reality farther than a frontal contest over who is stronger. In a deadlock, find the smallest change both sides can accept and let its result guide the next step; a modest entrance lowers defense and produces real evidence.
Softness does not erase boundaries. The tone can be gentle while the principle remains clear; lowering confrontation gives the other person a chance to hear the content. State the specific behavior, impact, and consequence without condemning the whole person; a gentle tone joined to clear structure keeps a boundary from sounding optional.
Make change a continuous influence rather than one explosion. Stable feedback, repeated example, and small correction may look slow, yet they pass through defense and allow a new habit to remain in the system. If the goal truly matters, accept that it may require repeated adjustment rather than one conquest; patience preserves the people and trust needed for continuing work.

en.title: Transformation Without Forcing
verse: The Tao in its regular course does nothing (for the sake of doing it), and so there is nothing which it does not do.
If princes and kings were able to maintain it, all things would of themselves be transformed by them.
If this transformation became to me an object of desire, I would express the desire by the nameless simplicity.
Simplicity without a name Is free from all external aim.
With no desire, at rest and still, All things go right as of their will.

explanation.title: Plain reading · Read the movement of the whole chapter
explanation.body: Beginning from “道恒无名，侯王若能守之，,” this chapter explores transformation without forcing. It does not demand a rigid answer; it asks how conditions, opposites, limits, and timing change what wise action looks like.

explanation.title: Chapter theme
explanation.body: Not every improvement comes from more management. Once essential boundaries are clear, less interference and more room for self-correction can create a steadier order than constant adjustment.

related.title: What this teaches us
related.body:
Not every improvement requires more management. Once purpose, boundaries, and responsibility are clear, less intervention allows people to adjust through feedback and build capacity. Clarify purpose, boundaries, and review intervals, then stop directing every step; non-interference is responsible only when autonomous adjustment can actually be observed.
A manager must tolerate a process that does not reproduce their exact style. When risk is controlled and the purpose is served, allow different methods; diversity is a reserve for adaptation. Even with less intervention, continue watching power imbalance and real harm, protecting where necessary; refusing manipulation does not mean ignoring difficulty faced by the vulnerable.
When order repeatedly depends on reminders and supervision, inspect the design. Clearer information, faster feedback, and responsibility closer to the work help more than adding another person whose job is to chase everyone. When a system operates steadily, resist adding management for visibility; use results to decide whether intervention is needed and give human capacity time to settle.
